title: The Gettysburg Address
author: Abraham Lincoln

sentences.en: Four score and seven years ago our fathers brought forth on this continent, a new nation, conceived in Liberty…
sentences.zh: 八十七年前，我们的先辈在这块大陆上建立了一个新的国家，它孕育于自由之中……

sentences.en: …and dedicated to the proposition that all men are created equal.
sentences.zh: ……并致力于这样一项信念：人人生而平等。

sentences.en: Now we are engaged in a great civil war…
sentences.zh: 如今我们正投身于一场伟大的内战……

sentences.en: …testing whether that nation, or any nation so conceived and so dedicated, can long endure.
sentences.zh: ……以检验这个国家，或任何如此孕育、如此奉行的国家，能否长久存续。

sentences.en: We are met on a great battle-field of that war.
sentences.zh: 我们在这场战争的一个伟大战场上相聚。

sentences.en: It is altogether fitting and proper that we should do this.
sentences.zh: 我们这样做，是完全合适而恰当的。

sentences.en: The world will little note, nor long remember what we say here, but it can never forget what they did here.
sentences.zh: 世人不会太留意，也不会长久记住我们在这里说过的话，却永远不会忘记他们在这里做过的事。

sentences.en: …and that government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.
sentences.zh: ……而这个民有、民治、民享的政府绝不会从地球上消亡。

source: Abraham Lincoln, The Gettysburg Address (1863). 公版作品（美国联邦政府文本，无版权）。节选：原句过长处按分句截断并以省略号标注。

title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
author: Alan Turing

sentences.en: I propose to consider the question, 'Can machines think?'
sentences.zh: 我提议讨论这样一个问题：“机器能思考吗？”

sentences.en: This should begin with definitions of the meaning of the terms 'machine' and 'think'.
sentences.zh: 这应当从界定“机器”和“思考”这两个词的含义开始。

sentences.en: The definitions might be framed so as to reflect so far as possible the normal use of the words…
sentences.zh: 这些定义可以尽量贴近这两个词的日常用法来构造……

sentences.en: …but this attitude is dangerous.
sentences.zh: ……但这样的态度是危险的。

sentences.en: The new form of the problem can be described in terms of a game which we call the 'imitation game'.
sentences.zh: 这个问题的新形式，可以用一种我们称之为“模仿游戏”的游戏来描述。

sentences.en: It is played with three people, a man (A), a woman (B), and an interrogator (C) who may be of either sex.
sentences.zh: 游戏由三个人进行：一名男子（A）、一名女子（B），以及一位性别不限的提问者（C）。

sentences.en: The interrogator stays in a room apart from the other two.
sentences.zh: 提问者待在与另外两人分开的房间里。

sentences.en: The object of the game for the interrogator is to determine which of the other two is the man and which is the woman.
sentences.zh: 提问者的目标是判断另外两人中谁是男子、谁是女子。

source: Alan Turing, “Computing Machinery and Intelligence”, Mind, 1950. 公版作品（作者 1954 年去世，著作权保护期已届满）。节选：开篇与模仿游戏设定。

title: The World As I See It
author: Albert Einstein

sentences.en: What an extraordinary situation is that of us mortals!
sentences.zh: 我们这些凡人所处的境况，是多么奇特啊！

sentences.en: Each of us is here for a brief sojourn; for what purpose he knows not, though he sometimes thinks he feels it.
sentences.zh: 我们每个人来此只是短暂停留；究竟为了什么，他并不知道，尽管他有时自以为感受到了。

sentences.en: Without deeper reflection one knows from daily life that one exists for other people…
sentences.zh: 无需深思，从日常生活中就能明白：人是为别人而存在的……

sentences.en: …first of all for those upon whose smiles and well-being our own happiness is wholly dependent…
sentences.zh: ……首先是为那些人的微笑与幸福而存在，我们自己的幸福完全系于此……

sentences.en: …and then for the many, unknown to us, to whose destinies we are bound by the ties of sympathy.
sentences.zh: ……其次是为那许多素不相识的人，我们因同情的纽带而与他们的命运相连。

sentences.en: A hundred times a day I remind myself that my inner and outer life are based on the labors of other men…
sentences.zh: 每天我都会上百次地提醒自己：我的内在生活与外在生活，都建立在他人——无论在世或已故——的劳动之上……

sentences.en: …living and dead, and that I must exert myself in order to give in the same measure…
sentences.zh: ……以及我必须努力，以便按同样的分量去回报……

sentences.en: …as I have received and am still receiving.
sentences.zh: ……回报我已得到、并仍在得到的那些。

source: Albert Einstein, “The World As I See It” (Mein Weltbild, 1934; 英译 Alan Harris). 公版作品。节选：开篇关于人与他人关系的段落，长句按分句截断并以省略号标注。

title: Sonnet 18
author: William Shakespeare

sentences.en: Shall I compare thee to a summer’s day?
sentences.zh: 我能否把你比作夏日？

sentences.en: Thou art more lovely and more temperate:
sentences.zh: 你比夏日更可爱，也更温和：

sentences.en: Rough winds do shake the darling buds of May,
sentences.zh: 狂风会摇落五月娇嫩的花蕾，

sentences.en: And summer’s lease hath all too short a date;
sentences.zh: 而夏天的租期又实在太短促；

sentences.en: Sometime too hot the eye of heaven shines,
sentences.zh: 有时那天上的眼睛照得太热，

sentences.en: And often is his gold complexion dimmed;
sentences.zh: 他金色的面容又常常黯淡；

sentences.en: And every fair from fair sometime declines,
sentences.zh: 一切美好终有凋零之时，

sentences.en: By chance or nature’s changing course untrimmed;
sentences.zh: 或因偶然，或因自然无常的流转；

sentences.en: But thy eternal summer shall not fade,
sentences.zh: 但你那永恒的夏天永远不会褪色，

sentences.en: Nor lose possession of that fair thou ow’st;
sentences.zh: 也不会失去你所拥有的那份美好；

source: William Shakespeare, Sonnet 18 (1609). 公版作品。节选第 1–10 行（共 14 行）。拼写按现代通行本（如 dimmed / untrimmed），标点一仍其旧。

title: Stay Hungry, Stay Foolish
author: Steve Jobs

sentences.en: In 2005 Jobs told the Stanford graduating class three stories from his own life.
sentences.zh: 2005 年，乔布斯在斯坦福大学毕业典礼上讲了三个关于他自己人生的故事。

sentences.en: The first story was about trusting that the dots of your life will connect later on.
sentences.zh: 第一个故事讲的是：要相信人生中的那些点，日后自会连成一线。

sentences.en: You cannot connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backwards.
sentences.zh: 你无法在向前看时把生命中的点连起来，只有在回望时才能把它们连起来。

sentences.en: He then turned to death, saying that facing it had helped him make the big choices in life.
sentences.zh: 接着他谈到死亡，说正视死亡帮助他做出了人生中的重大选择。

sentences.en: Remembering that you are going to die is the best way I know to avoid the trap of thinking you have something to lose.
sentences.zh: 记住自己终将死去，是我所知避免陷入“自己有什么可失去”这一陷阱的最好办法。

sentences.en: Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life.
sentences.zh: 你的时间有限，所以不要浪费时间去过别人的生活。

sentences.en: Stay hungry, stay foolish.
sentences.zh: 求知若饥，虚心若愚。

source: Steve Jobs, Stanford University Commencement Address, 12 June 2005. 公开演讲，非公版。按任务要求：**逐字引用不超过 4 句**（第 3、5、6、7 句），其余（第 1、2、4 句）为准确的自我转述，不复述长段原文。

title: Politics and the English Language
author: George Orwell

sentences.en: Most people who bother with the matter at all would admit that the English language is in a bad way…
sentences.zh: 凡是稍微关心这件事的人，大多会承认英语的状况不妙……

sentences.en: A man may take to drink because he feels himself to be a failure…
sentences.zh: 一个人可能因为觉得自己是个失败者而开始酗酒……

sentences.en: …and then fail all the more completely because he drinks.
sentences.zh: ……然后又因为酗酒而败得更彻底。

sentences.en: It is rather the same thing that is happening to the English language.
sentences.zh: 英语正在发生的情况，与此颇有相似之处。

sentences.en: The point is that the process is reversible.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，这个过程是可以逆转的。

sentences.en: If thought corrupts language, language can also corrupt thought.
sentences.zh: 如果思想败坏语言，语言同样也能败坏思想。

sentences.en: A bad usage can spread by tradition and imitation…
sentences.zh: 错误的用法会经由传统与模仿传播开来……

sentences.en: The great enemy of clear language is insincerity.
sentences.zh: 清晰语言的大敌，是言不由衷。

source: George Orwell, “Politics and the English Language” (1946). 公版作品（作者 1950 年去世，著作权保护期已届满）。节选：开篇诊断与结尾论断，长句按分句截断并以省略号标注。

title: The Bat and the Weasels
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Bat fell to the ground and was caught by a Weasel, and was just going to be killed and eaten when it begged to be let go.
sentences.zh: 一只蝙蝠掉到地上，被黄鼠狼捉住了。眼看就要被弄死吃掉，它哀求放它一条生路。

sentences.en: The Weasel said he couldn't do that because he was an enemy of all birds on principle.
sentences.zh: 黄鼠狼说这不行，因为他天生就是一切鸟类的敌人。

sentences.en: "Oh, but," said the Bat, "I'm not a bird at all: I'm a mouse."
sentences.zh: “哦，可我不是鸟啊，”蝙蝠说，“我是老鼠。”

sentences.en: "So you are," said the Weasel, "now I come to look at you"; and he let it go.
sentences.zh: “可不是嘛，”黄鼠狼说，“这么一瞧，还真是。”于是把它放了。

sentences.en: Some time after this the Bat was caught in just the same way by another Weasel, and, as before, begged for its life.
sentences.zh: 过了些日子，蝙蝠又以同样的方式被另一只黄鼠狼捉住，它照旧求饶保命。

sentences.en: "No," said the Weasel, "I never let a mouse go by any chance."
sentences.zh: “不行，”黄鼠狼说，“我从不放过任何一只老鼠。”

sentences.en: "But I'm not a mouse," said the Bat; "I'm a bird."
sentences.zh: “可我不是老鼠，”蝙蝠说，“我是鸟。”

sentences.en: "Why, so you are," said the Weasel; and he too let the Bat go.
sentences.zh: “咦，还真是。”黄鼠狼说着，也把蝙蝠放了。

sentences.en: Look and see which way the wind blows before you commit yourself.
sentences.zh: 先看清风向，再决定自己站哪一边。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Dog, the Cock, and the Fox
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Dog and a Cock became great friends, and agreed to travel together.
sentences.zh: 一条狗和一只公鸡成了好朋友，说好一起出门远行。

sentences.en: At nightfall the Cock flew up into the branches of a tree to roost, while the Dog curled himself up inside the trunk, which was hollow.
sentences.zh: 天黑时，公鸡飞上树枝栖息，狗就蜷在空心的树干里。

sentences.en: At break of day the Cock woke up and crew, as usual.
sentences.zh: 天一亮，公鸡醒来，照例打起鸣来。

sentences.en: A Fox heard, and, wishing to make a breakfast of him, came and stood under the tree and begged him to come down.
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸听见了，想拿它当早饭，便走到树下，请公鸡下来。

sentences.en: "I should so like," said he, "to make the acquaintance of one who has such a beautiful voice."
sentences.zh: 狐狸说：“嗓子这么好的人，我真想结识一下。”

sentences.en: The Cock replied, "Would you just wake my porter who sleeps at the foot of the tree?
sentences.zh: 公鸡答道：“那你能不能先叫醒睡在树根那儿的门房？

sentences.en: He'll open the door and let you in."
sentences.zh: 他会开门让你进来的。”

sentences.en: The Fox accordingly rapped on the trunk, when out rushed the Dog and tore him in pieces.
sentences.zh: 狐狸便去敲树干，狗猛地冲出来，把它撕成了碎片。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Crab and His Mother
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Old Crab said to her son, "Why do you walk sideways like that, my son?
sentences.zh: 老螃蟹对儿子说：“孩子，你怎么老是横着走？

sentences.en: You ought to walk straight."
sentences.zh: 你该直着走才对。”

sentences.en: The Young Crab replied, "Show me how, dear mother, and I'll follow your example."
sentences.zh: 小螃蟹答道：“妈妈，您走给我看看，我照着学。”

sentences.en: The Old Crab tried, but tried in vain, and then saw how foolish she had been to find fault with her child.
sentences.zh: 老螃蟹试了又试，怎么也走不直，这才明白自己挑孩子的毛病是多么可笑。

sentences.en: Example is better than precept.
sentences.zh: 身教胜于言传。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Two Pots
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Two Pots, one of earthenware and the other of brass, were carried away down a river in flood.
sentences.zh: 一只陶罐和一只铜罐，被洪水冲下了河。

sentences.en: The Brazen Pot urged his companion to keep close by his side, and he would protect him.
sentences.zh: 铜罐劝同伴紧挨着自己走，说这样能护着它。

sentences.en: The other thanked him, but begged him not to come near him on any account: "For that," he said, "is just what I am most afraid of.
sentences.zh: 陶罐谢过它，却求它千万别靠近：“因为，”它说，“我最怕的正是这个。

sentences.en: One touch from you and I should be broken in pieces."
sentences.zh: 你只要碰我一下，我就碎了。”

sentences.en: Equals make the best friends.
sentences.zh: 势均力敌，才做得成好伙伴。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Grasshopper and the Ants
author: Aesop

sentences.en: One fine day in winter some Ants were busy drying their store of corn, which had got rather damp during a long spell of rain.
sentences.zh: 冬天的一个晴日，几只蚂蚁正忙着晾晒存粮——那场下了很久的雨把谷子浸得有些潮了。

sentences.en: Presently up came a Grasshopper and begged them to spare her a few grains, "For," she said, "I'm simply starving."
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，一只蚱蜢过来，求它们分几粒谷子给它：“我实在是饿坏了。”

sentences.en: The Ants stopped work for a moment, though this was against their principles.
sentences.zh: 蚂蚁们停下手里的活——虽然这有违它们一贯的做法。

sentences.en: "May we ask," said they, "what you were doing with yourself all last summer?
sentences.zh: 它们问：“能问问吗，去年整个夏天你都在做什么？

sentences.en: Why didn't you collect a store of food for the winter?"
sentences.zh: 怎么不攒点过冬的粮食呢？”

sentences.en: "The fact is," replied the Grasshopper, "I was so busy singing that I hadn't the time."
sentences.zh: 蚱蜢答道：“实话说，我忙着唱歌，没工夫。”

sentences.en: "If you spent the summer singing," replied the Ants, "you can't do better than spend the winter dancing."
sentences.zh: 蚂蚁们说：“夏天既然用来唱歌，那冬天跳舞就再合适不过了。”

sentences.en: And they chuckled and went on with their work.
sentences.zh: 说完，它们笑了笑，接着干活。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Hound and the Fox
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Hound, roaming in the forest, spied a lion, and being well used to lesser game, gave chase, thinking he would make a fine quarry.
sentences.zh: 一条猎犬在林子里游荡，望见一头狮子。它追惯了小家伙，便撵了上去，只当是碰上了好猎物。

sentences.en: Presently the lion perceived that he was being pursued; so, stopping short, he rounded on his pursuer and gave a loud roar.
sentences.zh: 狮子很快察觉有东西在追它，猛地停住，转身对着追兵大吼一声。

sentences.en: The Hound immediately turned tail and fled.
sentences.zh: 猎犬立刻掉头就跑。

sentences.en: A Fox, seeing him running away, jeered at him and said, "Ho! ho!
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸见它逃得狼狈，嘲笑说：“哟哟！

sentences.en: There goes the coward who chased a lion and ran away the moment he roared!"
sentences.zh: 这就是那位追狮子的好汉啊——狮子一吼，掉头就跑！”

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Wolf and the Horse
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Wolf on his rambles came to a field of oats, but, not being able to eat them, he was passing on his way when a Horse came along.
sentences.zh: 一只狼闲逛到一片燕麦地。它吃不了燕麦，正要走开，一匹马过来了。

sentences.en: "Look," said the Wolf, "here's a fine field of oats.
sentences.zh: “瞧，”狼说，“多好的一片燕麦。

sentences.en: For your sake I have left it untouched, and I shall greatly enjoy the sound of your teeth munching the ripe grain."
sentences.zh: 我是看你的面子才没动它。我倒是很想听听你嚼这熟谷子的声响。”

sentences.en: But the Horse replied, "If wolves could eat oats, my fine friend, you would hardly have indulged your ears at the cost of your belly."
sentences.zh: 马答道：“好朋友，狼要是能吃燕麦，你就不会为了饱耳福而饿肚子了。”

sentences.en: There is no virtue in giving to others what is useless to oneself.
sentences.zh: 把自己用不上的东西送给别人，算不上什么美德。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Frogs' Complaint Against the Sun
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Once upon a time the Sun was about to take to himself a wife.
sentences.zh: 从前，太阳打算娶妻。

sentences.en: The Frogs in terror all raised their voices to the skies, and Jupiter, disturbed by the noise, asked them what they were croaking about.
sentences.zh: 青蛙们吓坏了，齐声向天叫喊。朱庇特被吵得不得安宁，问它们究竟在呱呱叫什么。

sentences.en: They replied, "The Sun is bad enough even while he is single, drying up our marshes with his heat as he does.
sentences.zh: 它们答道：“太阳一个人就已经够受了，他这么一晒，把我们的沼泽都晒干了。

sentences.en: But what will become of us if he marries and begets other Suns?"
sentences.zh: 要是他娶了妻、又生出许多太阳来，我们可怎么活？”

title: The Hare and the Hound
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Hound started a Hare from her form, and pursued her for some distance; but as she gradually gained upon him, he gave up the chase.
sentences.zh: 一条猎犬把一只野兔从窝里轰了出来，追了一程；可野兔渐渐拉开了距离，它便放弃了。

sentences.en: A rustic who had seen the race met the Hound as he was returning, and taunted him with his defeat.
sentences.zh: 一个瞧见这场追逐的乡下人，在猎犬往回走时遇上了它，便拿它的败绩打趣。

sentences.en: "The little one was too much for you," said he.
sentences.zh: 他说：“这么个小东西，你都奈何不了。”

sentences.en: "Ah, well," said the Hound, "don't forget it's one thing to be running for your dinner, but quite another to be running for your life."
sentences.zh: “唉，”猎犬说，“别忘了，为了一顿饭而跑是一回事，为了活命而跑是另一回事。”

title: The Stag and the Lion
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Stag was chased by the hounds, and took refuge in a cave, where he hoped to be safe from his pursuers.
sentences.zh: 一头雄鹿被猎犬追赶，躲进一个山洞，指望在那里能避开追兵。

sentences.en: Unfortunately the cave contained a Lion, to whom he fell an easy prey.
sentences.zh: 不巧洞里有一头狮子，它轻易就成了狮子的口中食。

sentences.en: "Unhappy that I am," he cried, "I am saved from the power of the dogs only to fall into the clutches of a Lion."
sentences.zh: 它叫道：“我好苦命！刚逃出狗的爪牙，又落进了狮子的掌心。”

sentences.en: Out of the frying-pan into the fire.
sentences.zh: 才出煎锅，又入火坑。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Man and his Wife had the good fortune to possess a Goose which laid a Golden Egg every day.
sentences.zh: 有对夫妇运气好，养了一只每天下一个金蛋的鹅。

sentences.en: Lucky though they were, they soon began to think they were not getting rich fast enough, and, imagining the bird must be made of gold …
sentences.zh: 他们虽算走运，却很快嫌发财太慢，又猜想这鹅肚子里准是一整块金子……

sentences.en: … inside, they decided to kill it in order to secure the whole store of precious metal at once.
sentences.zh: ……于是一刀把鹅杀了，想一次把那些贵金属全拿到手。

sentences.en: But when they cut it open they found it was just like any other goose.
sentences.zh: 可剖开一看，这鹅跟别的鹅没什么两样。

sentences.en: Thus, they neither got rich all at once, as they had hoped, nor enjoyed any longer the daily addition to their wealth.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们既没能像盼望的那样一下子暴富，也再没有每天进项了。

sentences.en: Much wants more and loses all.
sentences.zh: 贪多反失。

title: The Mischievous Dog
author: Aesop

sentences.en: There was once a Dog who used to snap at people and bite them without any provocation …
sentences.zh: 从前有条狗，没人招惹它，它也动不动就扑上去咬人……

sentences.en: … and who was a great nuisance to every one who came to his master's house.
sentences.zh: ……凡是到主人家里来的人，都被它搅得不得安宁。

sentences.en: So his master fastened a bell round his neck to warn people of his presence.
sentences.zh: 于是主人在它脖子上系了个铃铛，好让人事先知道它来了。

sentences.en: The Dog was very proud of the bell, and strutted about tinkling it with immense satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 这狗却把铃铛当成了体面，走起路来趾高气扬，一路叮当作响，得意得很。

sentences.en: But an old dog came up to him and said, "The fewer airs you give yourself the better, my friend.
sentences.zh: 有条老狗走过来对它说：“朋友，你少摆点架子为好。

sentences.en: You don't think, do you, that your bell was given you as a reward of merit?
sentences.zh: 你总不会以为，这铃铛是赏你的功劳吧？

sentences.en: On the contrary, it is a badge of disgrace."
sentences.zh: 恰恰相反，那是块耻辱的标记。”

sentences.en: Notoriety is often mistaken for fame.
sentences.zh: 臭名常被误当美名。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Fox and the Crow
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Crow was sitting on a branch of a tree with a piece of cheese in her beak when a Fox observed her and set his wits to work to discover …
sentences.zh: 一只乌鸦衔着一块奶酪停在树枝上，被一只狐狸看见了。狐狸便动起脑筋，想找出……

sentences.en: … some way of getting the cheese.
sentences.zh: ……弄到那块奶酪的法子。

sentences.en: Coming and standing under the tree he looked up and said, "What a noble bird I see above me!
sentences.zh: 它走到树下站定，抬头道：“我头顶上这只鸟，可真高贵！

sentences.en: Her beauty is without equal, the hue of her plumage exquisite.
sentences.zh: 论美貌无人能比，这一身羽色更是精美。

sentences.en: If only her voice is as sweet as her looks are fair, she ought without doubt to be Queen of the Birds."
sentences.zh: 只要她的嗓音也像模样一样动人，那无疑就该做鸟中之王了。”

sentences.en: The Crow was hugely flattered by this, and just to show the Fox that she could sing she gave a loud caw.
sentences.zh: 乌鸦被夸得飘飘然，为了向狐狸证明自己能唱，就大声“嘎”了一声。

sentences.en: Down came the cheese, of course, and the Fox, snatching it up, said, "You have a voice, madam, I see: what you want is wits."
sentences.zh: 奶酪自然就掉了下来。狐狸一口叼起，说：“夫人，我看出来了，您有嗓子，缺的是脑子。”

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Cat and the Birds
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Cat heard that the Birds in an aviary were ailing.
sentences.zh: 一只猫听说鸟舍里的鸟都病了。

sentences.en: So he got himself up as a doctor, and, taking with him a set of the instruments proper to his profession, presented himself at the door …
sentences.zh: 它便打扮成医生的样子，带上这套行当该有的一套器具，来到鸟舍门口……

sentences.en: … and inquired after the health of the Birds.
sentences.zh: ……问候起鸟儿们的病情。

sentences.en: "We shall do very well," they replied, without letting him in, "when we've seen the last of you."
sentences.zh: “我们好得很，”鸟儿们没让它进门，答道，“等你走远了就好。”

sentences.en: A villain may disguise himself, but he will not deceive the wise.
sentences.zh: 恶人可以乔装，却骗不过明白人。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Wolf in Sheep's Clothing
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Wolf resolved to disguise himself in order that he might prey upon a flock of sheep without fear of detection.
sentences.zh: 一只狼打定主意要乔装一番，好去祸害羊群而不被察觉。

sentences.en: So he clothed himself in a sheepskin, and slipped among the sheep when they were out at pasture.
sentences.zh: 它披上一张羊皮，趁羊群在外放牧时混了进去。

sentences.en: He completely deceived the shepherd, and when the flock was penned for the night he was shut in with the rest.
sentences.zh: 它把牧人骗得死死的，晚上羊群入圈时，它也跟着一起被关了进去。

sentences.en: But that very night as it happened, the shepherd, requiring a supply of mutton for the table, laid hands on the Wolf in mistake for a …
sentences.zh: 可就在那天夜里，牧人要做菜，需要一只羊，错手抓起了这只狼……

sentences.en: … Sheep, and killed him with his knife on the spot.
sentences.zh: ……当成羊，当场一刀把它宰了。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Fir-Tree and the Bramble
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Fir-tree was boasting to a Bramble, and said, somewhat contemptuously, "You poor creature, you are of no use whatever.
sentences.zh: 一棵枞树向荆棘夸口，语气里颇有些不屑：“你这可怜东西，一点用处都没有。

sentences.en: Now, look at me: I am useful for all sorts of things, particularly when men build houses; they can't do without me then."
sentences.zh: 你看看我：我样样都用得上，尤其是人盖房的时候，离了我就没法动工。”

sentences.en: But the Bramble replied, "Ah, that's all very well …
sentences.zh: 荆棘却答道：“啊，这话说得倒好听……

sentences.en: … but you wait till they come with axes and saws to cut you down, and then you'll wish you were a Bramble and not a Fir."
sentences.zh: ……可你等着吧，等他们拎着斧子锯子来砍你的时候，你就宁愿自己是荆棘，不是枞树了。”

sentences.en: Better poverty without a care than wealth with its many obligations.
sentences.zh: 无牵无挂的穷，胜过拖累缠身的富。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Gnat and the Bull
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Gnat alighted on one of the horns of a Bull, and remained sitting there for a considerable time.
sentences.zh: 一只蚋落在公牛的角上，在那儿待了好一阵子。

sentences.en: When it had rested sufficiently and was about to fly away, it said to the Bull, "Do you mind if I go now?"
sentences.zh: 等歇够了要走的时候，它问公牛：“我现在走，你不介意吧？”

sentences.en: The Bull merely raised his eyes and remarked, without interest, "It's all one to me …
sentences.zh: 公牛只是抬了抬眼皮，淡淡地说：“对我来说都一样……

sentences.en: … I didn't notice when you came, and I shan't know when you go away."
sentences.zh: ……你来的时候我没留意，你走的时候我也不会知道。”

sentences.en: We may often be of more consequence in our own eyes than in the eyes of our neighbours.
sentences.zh: 我们常常把自己看得比在别人眼中重要得多。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Lamp
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lamp, well filled with oil, burned with a clear and steady light …
sentences.zh: 一盏油灯灌得满满的，烧出一团清亮而稳定的光……

sentences.en: … and began to swell with pride and boast that it shone more brightly than the sun himself.
sentences.zh: ……它便渐渐得意起来，夸口说自己比太阳还亮。

sentences.en: Just then a puff of wind came and blew it out.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，一阵风吹来，把它吹灭了。

sentences.en: Some one struck a match and lit it again, and said, "You just keep alight, and never mind the sun.
sentences.zh: 有人划了根火柴重新点亮它，说：“你只管亮着就好，别去管太阳。

sentences.en: Why, even the stars never need to be relit as you had to be just now."
sentences.zh: 人家星星可从来不用像你刚才那样，还得再点一次。”

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Ass in the Lion's Skin
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Ass found a Lion's Skin, and dressed himself up in it.
sentences.zh: 一头驴捡到一张狮皮，就披在了身上。

sentences.en: Then he went about frightening every one he met, for they all took him to be a lion, men and beasts alike …
sentences.zh: 然后它四处走动，见谁吓谁——人和兽都把它当成了狮子……

sentences.en: … and took to their heels when they saw him coming.
sentences.zh: ……一看见它过来就撒腿跑。

sentences.en: Elated by the success of his trick, he loudly brayed in triumph.
sentences.zh: 这招得逞，驴得意忘形，扯着嗓子大叫起来。

sentences.en: The Fox heard him, and recognised him at once for the Ass he was, and said to him, "Oho, my friend, it's you, is it?
sentences.zh: 狐狸听见了，立刻认出它是头驴，便说：“哦哟，朋友，原来是你呀？

sentences.en: I, too, should have been afraid if I hadn't heard your voice."
sentences.zh: 要不是听见你这嗓子，我本来也会怕的。”

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Boy Bathing
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Boy was bathing in a river and got out of his depth, and was in great danger of being drowned.
sentences.zh: 一个男孩在河里洗澡，不知不觉到了深处，眼看就要淹死。

sentences.en: A man who was passing along a road heard his cries for help …
sentences.zh: 有人从路上经过，听见他呼救……

sentences.en: … and went to the riverside and began to scold him for being so careless as to get into deep water, but made no attempt to help him.
sentences.zh: ……便走到岸边，责备他太不小心，居然走到深水里去，却一点也没有要救他的意思。

sentences.en: "Oh, sir," cried the Boy, "please help me first and scold me afterwards."
sentences.zh: “哎，先生，”男孩喊道，“求您先救我，再骂我吧。”

sentences.en: Give assistance, not advice, in a crisis.
sentences.zh: 危急关头要的是搭把手，不是讲道理。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Quack Frog
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Once upon a time a Frog came forth from his home in the marshes and proclaimed to all the world that he was a learned physician, skilled …
sentences.zh: 从前，一只青蛙从沼泽里的家出来，向世人宣称自己是个博学的医生，精通……

sentences.en: … in drugs and able to cure all diseases.
sentences.zh: ……药理，什么病都能治好。

sentences.en: Among the crowd was a Fox, who called out, "You a doctor!
sentences.zh: 人群里有只狐狸，高声说：“你，当医生！

sentences.en: Why, how can you set up to heal others when you cannot even cure your own lame legs and blotched and wrinkled skin?"
sentences.zh: 你自己那两条瘸腿、那一身斑斑驳驳的皱皮都治不好，怎么还张罗着给别人治病？”

sentences.en: Physician, heal thyself.
sentences.zh: 医生，先治治你自己吧。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Oxen and the Axletrees
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A pair of Oxen were drawing a heavily loaded waggon along the highway, and, as they tugged and strained at the yoke, the Axletrees …
sentences.zh: 两头牛拉着满载的大车走在路上。它们使劲拽着轭，车轴却……

sentences.en: … creaked and groaned terribly.
sentences.zh: ……吱吱呀呀叫得厉害。

sentences.en: This was too much for the Oxen, who turned round indignantly and said, "Hullo, you there!
sentences.zh: 牛实在忍不住了，气愤地回过头说：“喂，你们这些家伙！

sentences.en: Why do you make such a noise when we do all the work?"
sentences.zh: 活都是我们干的，你们叫唤什么？”

sentences.en: They complain most who suffer least.
sentences.zh: 叫得最响的，往往是吃苦最少的。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Man and the Lion
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Man and a Lion were companions on a journey, and in the course of conversation they began to boast about their prowess …
sentences.zh: 一个人和一头狮子结伴同行，聊着聊着，就各自夸起自己的本事来……

sentences.en: … and each claimed to be superior to the other in strength and courage.
sentences.zh: ……都说自己在力气和胆量上胜过对方。

sentences.en: They were still arguing with some heat when they came to a cross-road where there was a statue of a Man strangling a Lion.
sentences.zh: 两人正争得面红耳赤，走到一个路口，那里立着一座人掐死狮子的雕像。

sentences.en: "There!" said the Man triumphantly, "look at that!
sentences.zh: “瞧！”人得意地说，“看见没有！

sentences.en: Doesn't that prove to you that we are stronger than you?"
sentences.zh: 这还不说明我们比你们强吗？”

sentences.en: "Not so fast, my friend," said the Lion: "that is only your view of the case.
sentences.zh: “别急，朋友，”狮子说，“那不过是你们那边的说法。

sentences.en: If we Lions could make statues, you may be sure that in most of them you would see the Man underneath."
sentences.zh: 要是我们狮子会雕像，你准会看到，多半的像底下躺着的都是人。”

sentences.en: There are two sides to every question.
sentences.zh: 凡事都有两面。

title: The Wild Boar and the Fox
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Wild Boar was engaged in whetting his tusks upon the trunk of a tree in the forest when a Fox came by and, seeing what he was at, said …
sentences.zh: 一头野猪正在林子里对着树干磨牙。一只狐狸走过来，看见它这样，便说……

sentences.en: … to him, "Why are you doing that, pray?
sentences.zh: ……“请问，你这是做什么？

sentences.en: The huntsmen are not out to-day, and there are no other dangers at hand that I can see."
sentences.zh: 猎人今天没出来，我也看不出眼下有什么危险。”

sentences.en: "True, my friend," replied the Boar, "but the instant my life is in danger I shall need to use my tusks.
sentences.zh: “不错，朋友，”野猪答道，“可一旦性命有危险，我就得用上这牙了。

sentences.en: There'll be no time to sharpen them then."
sentences.zh: 到那时候，可就没工夫磨了。”

title: The Man and the Image
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A poor Man had a wooden Image of a god, to which he used to pray daily for riches.
sentences.zh: 有个穷人供着一尊木雕神像，天天求它赐财。

sentences.en: He did this for a long time, but remained as poor as ever, till one day he caught up the Image in disgust and hurled it with all his …
sentences.zh: 求了很久，他依旧穷得和从前一样。有一天他实在厌烦了，抓起神像，用尽全力……

sentences.en: … strength against the wall.
sentences.zh: ……朝墙上砸去。

sentences.en: The force of the blow split open the head and a quantity of gold coins fell out upon the floor.
sentences.zh: 这一下砸得神像的脑袋裂开，一大堆金币掉到了地上。

sentences.en: The Man gathered them up greedily, and said, "O you old fraud, you!
sentences.zh: 那人贪婪地把金币捡起来，说：“哼，你这老骗子！

sentences.en: When I honoured you, you did me no good whatever: but no sooner do I treat you to insults and violence than you make a rich man of me!"
sentences.zh: 我敬着你的时候，你一点好处也不给我；我这才对你又打又骂，你倒让我发了财！”

title: The Image-Seller
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A certain man made a wooden Image of Mercury, and exposed it for sale in the market.
sentences.zh: 有个人做了一尊墨丘利的木像，摆到市场上出卖。

sentences.en: As no one offered to buy it, however, he thought he would try to attract a purchaser by proclaiming the virtues of the Image.
sentences.zh: 可是没人肯买。他便想出一招：把这神像的好处大肆宣扬，好招徕买主。

sentences.en: So he cried up and down the market, "A god for sale! a god for sale!
sentences.zh: 于是他在市场里来回吆喝：“卖神啦！卖神啦！

sentences.en: One who'll bring you luck and keep you lucky!"
sentences.zh: 这神能给你带来好运，还能保你一直走运！”

sentences.en: Presently one of the bystanders stopped him and said, "If your god is all you make him out to be, how is it you don't keep him and make …
sentences.zh: 有个旁观者叫住他，说：“你这神要真像你说的那么好，你怎么不自己留着……

sentences.en: … the most of him yourself?"
sentences.zh: ……好好受用呢？”

sentences.en: "I'll tell you why," replied he; "he brings gain, it is true, but he takes his time about it; whereas I want money at once."
sentences.zh: 他答道：“告诉你为什么吧：它确实能带来好处，可它慢得很；我要的是现钱。”

title: The Eagle and the Arrow
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Eagle sat perched on a lofty rock, keeping a sharp look-out for prey.
sentences.zh: 一只鹰停在髙岩上，锐利地搜寻着猎物。

sentences.en: A huntsman, concealed in a cleft of the mountain and on the watch for game, spied him there and shot an Arrow at him.
sentences.zh: 一个猎人藏在山缝里等着猎物，瞧见了它，便朝它射了一箭。

sentences.en: The shaft struck him full in the breast and pierced him through and through.
sentences.zh: 这一箭正中心口，把它射了个对穿。

sentences.en: As he lay in the agonies of death, he turned his eyes upon the Arrow.
sentences.zh: 它痛苦地躺在那儿等死，眼睛却望向那支箭。

sentences.en: "Ah! cruel fate!" he cried, "that I should perish thus …
sentences.zh: “啊！好狠的命！”它叫道，“我竟这样死去……

sentences.en: … but oh! fate more cruel still, that the Arrow which kills me should be winged with an Eagle's feathers!"
sentences.zh: ……可哎！命更狠的是，要了我命的这支箭，箭尾上插的竟是鹰的羽毛！”

title: The Lioness and the Vixen
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lioness and a Vixen were talking together about their young, as mothers will, and saying how healthy and well-grown they were …
sentences.zh: 母狮和母狐凑在一起，像做母亲的那样聊起各自的孩子，说它们多健壮、长得多好……

sentences.en: … and what beautiful coats they had, and how they were the image of their parents.
sentences.zh: ……毛色多漂亮，活脱脱就是父母的翻版。

sentences.en: "My litter of cubs is a joy to see," said the Fox; and then she added, rather maliciously, "But I notice you never have more than one."
sentences.zh: “我一窝小崽，看着就叫人高兴，”狐狸说；接着又带几分恶意地补了一句，“不过我留意到，你从来只生一个。”

sentences.en: "No," said the Lioness grimly, "but that one's a lion."
sentences.zh: “是啊，”母狮冷冷地说，“可那一个是狮子。”

sentences.en: Quality, not quantity.
sentences.zh: 贵在质，不在量。

title: The Viper and the File
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Viper entered a carpenter's shop, and went from one to another of the tools, begging for something to eat.
sentences.zh: 一条蝰蛇爬进木匠铺，挨个向里面的工具讨吃的。

sentences.en: Among the rest, he addressed himself to the File, and asked for the favour of a meal.
sentences.zh: 轮到锉刀时，它开口请求赏它一顿饭。

sentences.en: The File replied in a tone of pitying contempt, "What a simpleton you must be if you imagine you will get anything from me …
sentences.zh: 锉刀带着几分怜悯的轻蔑答道：“你要是以为能从我这儿得到什么，那可真是傻透了……

sentences.en: … who invariably take from every one and never give anything in return."
sentences.zh: ……我向来只从别人身上取，从不回报什么。”

sentences.en: The covetous are poor givers.
sentences.zh: 贪得的人，给不出什么。

title: The Horse and His Rider
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Young Man, who fancied himself something of a horseman, mounted a Horse which had not been properly broken in …
sentences.zh: 有个年轻人自以为算个骑手，骑上了一匹还没调教好的马……

sentences.en: … and was exceedingly difficult to control.
sentences.zh: ……那马极难驾驭。

sentences.en: No sooner did the Horse feel his weight in the saddle than he bolted, and nothing would stop him.
sentences.zh: 马一感到鞍上有了重量，撒开蹄子就跑，什么都拦不住。

sentences.en: A friend of the Rider's met him in the road in his headlong career, and called out, "Where are you off to in such a hurry?"
sentences.zh: 骑手的一个朋友在路上撞见他这般狂奔，喊道：“你这么急急忙忙，是要去哪儿？”

sentences.en: To which he, pointing to the Horse, replied, "I've no idea: ask him."
sentences.zh: 他指着那匹马答道：“我哪知道，你问它。”

title: The Goat and the Vine
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Goat was straying in a vineyard, and began to browse on the tender shoots of a Vine which bore several fine bunches of grapes.
sentences.zh: 一只山羊在葡萄园里游荡，啃起一株葡萄藤的嫩芽——那藤上还挂着好几串好葡萄。

sentences.en: "What have I done to you," said the Vine, "that you should harm me thus?
sentences.zh: “我哪里得罪你了，”葡萄藤说，“你要这样糟蹋我？

sentences.en: Isn't there grass enough for you to feed on?
sentences.zh: 难道就没有足够的草给你吃吗？

sentences.en: All the same, even if you eat up every leaf I have …
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，就算你把我叶子吃个精光……

sentences.en: … and leave me quite bare, I shall produce wine enough to pour over you when you are led to the altar to be sacrificed."
sentences.zh: ……把我啃得光秃秃的，我也照样能酿出酒来，足够在你被牵上祭坛宰掉时浇在你身上。”

title: The Hound and the Hare
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A young Hound started a Hare, and, when he caught her up, would at one moment snap at her with his teeth as though he were about to kill …
sentences.zh: 一条小猎犬把一只野兔赶了出来，追上时就张嘴咬它，像是要弄死它……

sentences.en: … her, while at another he would let go his hold and frisk about her, as if he were playing with another dog.
sentences.zh: ……可一会儿又松开嘴，围着它撒欢，像是跟另一条狗在玩耍。

sentences.en: At last the Hare said, "I wish you would show yourself in your true colours!
sentences.zh: 野兔终于说：“你能不能露出真面目来！

sentences.en: If you are my friend, why do you bite me?
sentences.zh: 你要是我的朋友，为什么咬我？

sentences.en: If you are my enemy, why do you play with me?"
sentences.zh: 你要是我的敌人，为什么又跟我玩？”

sentences.en: He is no friend who plays double.
sentences.zh: 两面三刀的，不是朋友。

title: The Wolf and the Crane
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Wolf once got a bone stuck in his throat.
sentences.zh: 有一次，一根骨头卡在了狼的喉咙里。

sentences.en: So he went to a Crane and begged her to put her long bill down his throat and pull it out.
sentences.zh: 它便去找一只鹤，求她把长嘴伸进自己喉咙里把骨头叼出来。

sentences.en: "I'll make it worth your while," he added.
sentences.zh: 它还补了一句：“我不会让你白干的。”

sentences.en: The Crane did as she was asked, and got the bone out quite easily.
sentences.zh: 鹤照办了，很轻松就把骨头取了出来。

sentences.en: The Wolf thanked her warmly, and was just turning away, when she cried, "What about that fee of mine?"
sentences.zh: 狼热络地道了谢，正要转身走开，鹤叫道：“我那份酬劳呢？”

sentences.en: "Well, what about it?" snapped the Wolf, baring his teeth as he spoke …
sentences.zh: “什么酬劳？”狼龇着牙恶声说……

sentences.en: … "you can go about boasting that you once put your head into a Wolf's mouth and didn't get it bitten off.
sentences.zh: ……“你大可以到处去炫耀：你曾把脑袋伸进狼嘴里，还完好无损地拿了出来。

sentences.en: What more do you want?"
sentences.zh: 你还想要什么？”

title: The Three Tradesmen
author: Aesop

sentences.en: The citizens of a certain city were debating about the best material to use in the fortifications which were about to be erected for the …
sentences.zh: 某城的市民正在争论：即将修筑的防御工事，用什么材料最好……

sentences.en: … greater security of the town.
sentences.zh: ……好让城防更牢固。

sentences.en: A Carpenter got up and advised the use of wood, which he said was readily procurable and easily worked.
sentences.zh: 一个木匠站起来，主张用木头，说木料好弄，加工也方便。

sentences.en: A Stone-mason objected to wood on the ground that it was so inflammable, and recommended stones instead.
sentences.zh: 一个石匠反对用木头，理由是木头太容易着火，建议改用石头。

sentences.en: Then a Tanner got on his legs and said, "In my opinion there's nothing like leather."
sentences.zh: 接着一个皮匠站起身来，说：“依我看，什么也比不上皮革。”

sentences.en: Every man for himself.
sentences.zh: 人人只为自己打算。

title: The Eagle and the Cocks
author: Aesop

sentences.en: There were two Cocks in the same farmyard, and they fought to decide who should be master.
sentences.zh: 同一个农家院子里有两只公鸡，它们打了一架，要决出谁来做主。

sentences.en: When the fight was over, the beaten one went and hid himself in a dark corner …
sentences.zh: 斗完，输了的那只躲进一个暗角里……

sentences.en: … while the victor flew up on to the roof of the stables and crowed lustily.
sentences.zh: ……赢了的那只则飞上马棚顶，起劲地打起鸣来。

sentences.en: But an Eagle espied him from high up in the sky, and swooped down and carried him off.
sentences.zh: 可一只鹰从高空望见了它，俯冲下来把它抓走了。

sentences.en: Forthwith the other Cock came out of his corner and ruled the roost without a rival.
sentences.zh: 另一只公鸡立刻从角落里出来，从此独霸这个院子，再没对手。

sentences.en: Pride comes before a fall.
sentences.zh: 骄兵必败。

title: The Fly and the Draught-Mule
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Fly sat on one of the shafts of a cart and said to the Mule who was pulling it, "How slow you are!
sentences.zh: 一只苍蝇停在车辕上，对拉车的骡子说：“你走得真慢！

sentences.en: Do mend your pace, or I shall have to use my sting as a goad."
sentences.zh: 快些走，不然我只好把这根刺当鞭子用了。”

sentences.en: The Mule was not in the least disturbed.
sentences.zh: 骡子一点儿也没被它唬住。

sentences.en: "Behind me, in the cart," said he, "sits my master.
sentences.zh: “我身后这车上，”它说，“坐着我的主人。

sentences.en: He holds the reins, and flicks me with his whip, and him I obey …
sentences.zh: 他握着缰绳，用鞭子抽我，我听他的……

sentences.en: … but I don't want any of your impertinence. I know when I may dawdle and when I may not."
sentences.zh: ……可轮不到你来放肆。什么时候能磨蹭、什么时候不能，我自己清楚。”

title: The Charger and the Miller
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Horse, who had been used to carry his rider into battle, felt himself growing old and chose to work in a mill instead.
sentences.zh: 一匹马惯于驮着主人上阵，后来自觉老了，便改去磨坊干活。

sentences.en: He now no longer found himself stepping out proudly to the beating of the drums …
sentences.zh: 如今它再不能踏着鼓点昂首阔步……

sentences.en: … but was compelled to slave away all day grinding the corn.
sentences.zh: ……而是被迫整日像牛马一样拉着磨碾谷子。

sentences.en: Bewailing his hard lot, he said one day to the Miller, "Ah me!
sentences.zh: 有一天它向磨坊主叹起自己的苦命：“哎！

sentences.en: I was once a splendid war-horse, gaily caparisoned, and attended by a groom whose sole duty was to see to my wants.
sentences.zh: 我当年是多神气的战马，披着华丽的鞍辔，有专人侍候，那人唯一的差事就是照料我。

sentences.en: How different is my present condition!
sentences.zh: 如今这光景，真是天差地别！

sentences.en: I wish I had never given up the battlefield for the mill."
sentences.zh: 我真希望自己从没拿战场换过这座磨坊。”

sentences.en: The Miller replied with asperity, "It's no use your regretting the past.
sentences.zh: 磨坊主没好气地答道：“后悔过去有什么用。

sentences.en: Fortune has many ups and downs: you must just take them as they come."
sentences.zh: 运气本来就有起有落，来了什么，你就得受着什么。”

title: The Sick Man and the Doctor
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Sick Man received a visit from his Doctor, who asked him how he was.
sentences.zh: 一个病人有医生来看他，医生问他感觉如何。

sentences.en: "Fairly well, Doctor," said he, "but I find I sweat a great deal."
sentences.zh: “还好，大夫，”他说，“就是我发现自己出汗出得厉害。”

sentences.en: "Ah," said the Doctor, "that's a good sign."
sentences.zh: “啊，”医生说，“那是好兆头。”

sentences.en: On his next visit he asked the same question, and his patient replied, "I'm much as usual …
sentences.zh: 下一次来，医生又问了一遍，病人答道：“跟平常差不多……

sentences.en: … but I've taken to having shivering fits, which leave me cold all over."
sentences.zh: ……只是近来常打寒战，一阵下来浑身冰凉。”

sentences.en: "Ah," said the Doctor, "that's a good sign too."
sentences.zh: “啊，”医生说，“这也是好兆头。”

sentences.en: When he came the third time and inquired as before about his patient's health, the Sick Man said that he felt very feverish.
sentences.zh: 第三次来，他照旧询问病情，病人说自己烧得厉害。

sentences.en: "A very good sign," said the Doctor; "you are doing very nicely indeed."
sentences.zh: “很好的兆头，”医生说，“你恢复得确实不错。”

sentences.en: Afterwards a friend came to see the invalid, and on asking him how he did, received this reply: "My dear friend, I'm dying of good signs."
sentences.zh: 后来有位朋友来探望，问他怎么样，得到的回答是：“好朋友，我是被一堆好兆头给拖死的。”

title: The Lion and the Hare
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lion found a Hare sleeping in her form, and was just going to devour her when he caught sight of a passing stag.
sentences.zh: 一头狮子发现一只野兔在窝里睡觉，正要吃掉它，瞥见一头雄鹿走过。

sentences.en: Dropping the Hare, he at once made for the bigger game …
sentences.zh: 它丢下野兔，立刻去追那更大的猎物……

sentences.en: … but finding, after a long chase, that he could not overtake the stag, he abandoned the attempt and came back for the Hare.
sentences.zh: ……可追了许久，发现赶不上雄鹿，只好放弃，回头再去找那只野兔。

sentences.en: When he reached the spot, however, he found she was nowhere to be seen, and he had to go without his dinner.
sentences.zh: 然而到了那地方，野兔早已不见踪影，它只好空着肚子。

sentences.en: "It serves me right," he said; "I should have been content with what I had got, instead of hankering after a better prize."
sentences.zh: “这是我自找的，”它说，“我本该守着已经到手的东西，何必还惦记着更好的。”

title: The Wolves and the Dogs
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Once upon a time the Wolves said to the Dogs, "Why should we continue to be enemies any longer?
sentences.zh: 从前，狼对狗说：“我们何必还继续做仇敌？

sentences.en: You are very like us in most ways: the main difference between us is one of training only.
sentences.zh: 你们在多数方面都跟我们很像，彼此最大的差别只在于所受的调教。

sentences.en: We live a life of freedom; but you are enslaved to mankind, who beat you, and put heavy collars round your necks …
sentences.zh: 我们活得自由，你们却给人做奴隶：人打你们，把沉重的项圈套在你们脖子上……

sentences.en: … and compel you to keep watch over their flocks and herds for them, and, to crown all, they give you nothing but bones to eat.
sentences.zh: ……还逼你们替他们看守牛羊；最可气的是，他们只丢骨头给你们啃。

sentences.en: Don't put up with it any longer, but hand over the flocks to us, and we will all live on the fat of the land and feast together."
sentences.zh: 别再忍了，把羊群交给我们，咱们一起过好日子、一同享用。”

sentences.en: The Dogs allowed themselves to be persuaded by these words, and accompanied the Wolves into their den.
sentences.zh: 狗被这番话劝动了，跟着狼进了它们的窝。

sentences.en: But no sooner were they well inside than the Wolves set upon them and tore them to pieces.
sentences.zh: 可它们刚一进去，狼就扑上来，把它们撕成了碎片。

sentences.en: Traitors richly deserve their fate.
sentences.zh: 背叛者的下场，一点不冤。

title: The Trees and the Axe
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Woodman went into the forest and begged of the Trees the favour of a handle for his Axe.
sentences.zh: 一个樵夫走进林子，求树们给他一截做斧柄的木料。

sentences.en: The principal Trees at once agreed to so modest a request …
sentences.zh: 那些大树见要求不过分，立刻就答应了……

sentences.en: … and unhesitatingly gave him a young ash sapling, out of which he fashioned the handle he desired.
sentences.zh: ……毫不犹豫地给了他一株小梣树苗，他就用它做出了想要的斧柄。

sentences.en: No sooner had he done so than he set to work to fell the noblest Trees in the wood.
sentences.zh: 斧柄一装好，他立刻动手砍林子里最雄伟的那些树。

sentences.en: When they saw the use to which he was putting their gift, they cried, "Alas! alas!
sentences.zh: 树们见自己送出的东西被这样用，叫道：“唉！唉！

sentences.en: We are undone, but we are ourselves to blame.
sentences.zh: 我们完了，可这只能怪自己。

sentences.en: The little we gave has cost us all: had we not sacrificed the rights of the ash, we might ourselves have stood for ages."
sentences.zh: 我们让出那么一点，却赔上了全部：当初要不是牺牲了梣树的权利，我们本可以再立上几百年。”

title: The Ass and the Dog
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Ass and a Dog were on their travels together, and, as they went along, they found a sealed packet lying on the ground.
sentences.zh: 一头驴和一条狗结伴出门，走着走着，在地上捡到一个封了口的纸包。

sentences.en: The Ass picked it up, broke the seal, and found it contained some writing, which he proceeded to read out aloud to the Dog.
sentences.zh: 驴把它捡起来，拆开封口，见里面是些文字，便大声念给狗听。

sentences.en: As he read on it turned out to be all about grass and barley and hay--in short, all the kinds of fodder that Asses are fond of.
sentences.zh: 念下去才知道，通篇讲的都是草、大麦和干草——总之，全是驴爱吃的饲料。

sentences.en: The Dog was a good deal bored with listening to all this, till at last his impatience got the better of him …
sentences.zh: 狗听得十分腻烦，最后实在忍不住了……

sentences.en: … and he cried, "Just skip a few pages, friend, and see if there isn't something about meat and bones."
sentences.zh: ……叫道：“朋友，跳几页，看看有没有讲肉和骨头的。”

sentences.en: The Ass glanced all through the packet, but found nothing of the sort, and said so.
sentences.zh: 驴把整包翻了一遍，没找到这类内容，就照实说了。

sentences.en: Then the Dog said in disgust, "Oh, throw it away, do: what's the good of a thing like that?"
sentences.zh: 狗便厌恶地说：“嗨，扔了吧，这种东西有什么用？”

title: The Goatherd and the Goat
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Goatherd was one day gathering his flock to return to the fold, when one of his goats strayed and refused to join the rest.
sentences.zh: 一天，牧羊人正把羊群拢起来赶回圈里，有一只山羊却走散了，怎么也不肯归队。

sentences.en: He tried for a long time to get her to return by calling and whistling to her, but the Goat took no notice of him at all …
sentences.zh: 他又是喊又是吹口哨，试了很久想把它叫回来，那山羊却理都不理……

sentences.en: … so at last he threw a stone at her and broke one of her horns.
sentences.zh: ……他最后扔了块石头过去，打断了它一只角。

sentences.en: In dismay, he begged her not to tell his master: but she replied, "You silly fellow, my horn would cry aloud even if I held my tongue."
sentences.zh: 他慌了，求它别告诉主人；山羊却答道：“你这傻瓜，就算我不作声，我那只角也会喊出来的。”

sentences.en: It's no use trying to hide what can't be hidden.
sentences.zh: 藏不住的事，想遮也遮不住。

title: The Ploughman, the Ass, and the Ox
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Ploughman yoked his Ox and his Ass together, and set to work to plough his field.
sentences.zh: 一个农夫把牛和驴套在一副轭上，下地耕起田来。

sentences.en: It was a poor makeshift of a team, but it was the best he could do, as he had but a single Ox.
sentences.zh: 这一对搭得实在勉强，可他只有一头牛，也只能这样凑合。

sentences.en: At the end of the day, when the beasts were loosed from the yoke, the Ass said to the Ox, "Well, we've had a hard day …
sentences.zh: 一天下来，卸了轭，驴对牛说：“咱们今天可累坏了……

sentences.en: … which of us is to carry the master home?"
sentences.zh: ……回去的时候，咱们俩谁驮主人？”

sentences.en: The Ox looked surprised at the question.
sentences.zh: 牛听了这话，一脸诧异。

sentences.en: "Why," said he, "you, to be sure, as usual."
sentences.zh: “这还用问，”它说，“当然是你，一直都是你。”

title: The Wolf and His Shadow
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Wolf, who was roaming about on the plain when the sun was getting low in the sky, was much impressed by the size of his shadow …
sentences.zh: 太阳西沉时，一只狼在平原上闲荡，被自己影子的个头给镇住了……

sentences.en: … and said to himself, "I had no idea I was so big.
sentences.zh: ……它自言自语：“原来我这么大，我从前竟不知道。

sentences.en: Fancy my being afraid of a lion!
sentences.zh: 想想看，我居然还怕狮子！

sentences.en: Why, I, not he, ought to be King of the beasts"; and, heedless of danger, he strutted about as if there could be no doubt at all about it.
sentences.zh: 该做百兽之王的是我，不是它。”它全不把危险放在心上，大摇大摆地走着，仿佛这事已毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Just then a lion sprang upon him and began to devour him.
sentences.zh: 就在这时，一头狮子扑上来，开始撕咬它。

sentences.en: "Alas," he cried, "had I not lost sight of the facts, I shouldn't have been ruined by my fancies."
sentences.zh: “唉，”它叫道，“我要不是忘了实情，也不会被自己的幻想毁了。”

title: The Old Man and Death
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Old Man cut himself a bundle of faggots in a wood and started to carry them home.
sentences.zh: 一个老人在林子里砍了一捆柴，背着往家走。

sentences.en: He had a long way to go, and was tired out before he had got much more than half-way.
sentences.zh: 路还远，他走了不到一半就累垮了。

sentences.en: Casting his burden on the ground, he called upon Death to come and release him from his life of toil.
sentences.zh: 他把柴往地上一撂，呼唤死神快来，把他从这劳碌的生涯里解脱出去。

sentences.en: The words were scarcely out of his mouth when, much to his dismay, Death stood before him and professed his readiness to serve him.
sentences.zh: 话刚出口，死神就站到了他面前，说自己随时可以听候差遣。老人吓得不轻。

sentences.en: He was almost frightened out of his wits, but he had enough presence of mind to stammer out, "Good sir, if you'd be so kind, pray help me …
sentences.zh: 他几乎吓掉了魂，好在还稳得住，结结巴巴地说：“好先生，要是您肯帮忙，就请……

sentences.en: … up with my burden again."
sentences.zh: ……帮我把这担柴再架上肩吧。”

title: The Fox and the Bramble
author: Aesop

sentences.en: In making his way through a hedge a Fox missed his footing and caught at a Bramble to save himself from falling.
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸穿过树篱时脚下一滑，急忙抓住一丛荆棘，免得摔下去。

sentences.en: Naturally, he got badly scratched, and in disgust he cried to the Bramble, "It was your help I wanted, and see how you have treated me!
sentences.zh: 它自然被划得皮破血流，气恼地向荆棘叫道：“我是想让你帮一把，你看看你是怎么待我的！

sentences.en: I'd sooner have fallen outright."
sentences.zh: 我还不如干脆摔下去。”

sentences.en: The Bramble, interrupting him, replied, "You must have lost your wits, my friend, to catch at me …
sentences.zh: 荆棘打断它说：“朋友，你准是昏了头，才来抓我……

sentences.en: … who am myself always catching at others."
sentences.zh: ……我自己向来就是抓着别人不放的。”

title: The Swallow and the Crow
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Swallow was once boasting to a Crow about her birth.
sentences.zh: 有一次，一只燕子向乌鸦夸耀自己的出身。

sentences.en: "I was once a princess," said she, "the daughter of a King of Athens, but my husband used me cruelly …
sentences.zh: “我原是位公主，”她说，“雅典王的女儿；可我丈夫待我极狠……

sentences.en: … and cut out my tongue for a slight fault.
sentences.zh: ……只因一点小错，就把我的舌头割了。

sentences.en: Then, to protect me from further injury, I was turned by Juno into a bird."
sentences.zh: 后来为了免得我再受伤害，朱诺把我变成了一只鸟。”

sentences.en: "You chatter quite enough as it is," said the Crow.
sentences.zh: “就现在这样，你话也已经够多了，”乌鸦说。

sentences.en: "What you would have been like if you hadn't lost your tongue, I can't think."
sentences.zh: “要是舌头没丢，你该是什么样子，我真想不出来。”

title: The Man and the Satyr
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Man and a Satyr became friends, and determined to live together.
sentences.zh: 一个人和一个萨堤尔交上了朋友，决定住到一处。

sentences.en: All went well for a while, until one day in winter-time the Satyr saw the Man blowing on his hands.
sentences.zh: 起初一切都好。直到冬天里的一天，萨堤尔看见那人往自己手上呵气。

sentences.en: "Why do you do that?" he asked.
sentences.zh: “你这是做什么？”他问。

sentences.en: "To warm my hands," said the Man.
sentences.zh: “暖暖手。”那人说。

sentences.en: That same day, when they sat down to supper together, they each had a steaming hot bowl of porridge …
sentences.zh: 就在那天，两人坐下吃晚饭，各有一碗热腾腾的粥……

sentences.en: … and the Man raised his bowl to his mouth and blew on it.
sentences.zh: ……那人把碗端到嘴边，朝里头吹气。

sentences.en: "Why do you do that?" asked the Satyr.
sentences.zh: “你这又是做什么？”萨堤尔问。

sentences.en: "To cool my porridge," said the Man.
sentences.zh: “把粥吹凉。”那人说。

sentences.en: The Satyr got up from the table.
sentences.zh: 萨堤尔从桌边站起身来。

sentences.en: "Good-bye," said he, "I'm going: I can't be friends with a man who blows hot and cold with the same breath."
sentences.zh: “再见，”他说，“我走了。一个人用同一口气又吹热又吹凉，我没法跟他做朋友。”

title: The Parrot and the Cat
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Man once bought a Parrot and gave it the run of his house.
sentences.zh: 有人买了一只鹦鹉，让它在屋里随处走动。

sentences.en: It revelled in its liberty, and presently flew up on to the mantelpiece and screamed away to its heart's content.
sentences.zh: 鹦鹉得了自由，快活极了，不一会儿就飞到壁炉架上，放开嗓子叫了个痛快。

sentences.en: The noise disturbed the Cat, who was asleep on the hearthrug.
sentences.zh: 这声音吵着了睡在炉边地毯上的猫。

sentences.en: Looking up at the intruder, she said, "Who may you be, and where have you come from?"
sentences.zh: 猫抬头看着这个闯入者，说：“你是哪位？从哪儿来的？”

sentences.en: The Parrot replied, "Your master has just bought me and brought me home with him."
sentences.zh: 鹦鹉答道：“你家主人刚把我买回来，带我到了这儿。”

sentences.en: "You impudent bird," said the Cat, "how dare you, a newcomer, make a noise like that?
sentences.zh: “你这没规矩的鸟，”猫说，“新来的，怎么敢这么吵？

sentences.en: Why, I was born here, and have lived here all my life …
sentences.zh: 我可是生在这儿的，一辈子都住在这儿……

sentences.en: … and yet, if I venture to mew, they throw things at me and chase me all over the place."
sentences.zh: ……可我只要敢喵一声，他们就朝我扔东西，满屋子追我。”

sentences.en: "Look here, mistress," said the Parrot, "you just hold your tongue.
sentences.zh: “听我说，夫人，”鹦鹉说，“你闭上嘴就是了。

sentences.en: My voice they delight in; but yours--yours is a perfect nuisance."
sentences.zh: 他们爱听我唱；你那个嗓子——那才真叫惹人烦。”

title: The Lion, the Fox, and the Ass
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lion, a Fox, and an Ass went out hunting together.
sentences.zh: 狮子、狐狸和驴一同出去打猎。

sentences.en: They had soon taken a large booty, which the Lion requested the Ass to divide between them.
sentences.zh: 很快就收获了不少猎物，狮子让驴来给大家分。

sentences.en: The Ass divided it all into three equal parts, and modestly begged the others to take their choice …
sentences.zh: 驴把它平分成三份，客气地请另外两位先挑……

sentences.en: … at which the Lion, bursting with fury, sprang upon the Ass and tore him to pieces.
sentences.zh: 狮子勃然大怒，扑上去把驴撕成了碎片。

sentences.en: Then, glaring at the Fox, he bade him make a fresh division.
sentences.zh: 然后它瞪着狐狸，叫它重新分。

sentences.en: The Fox gathered almost the whole in one great heap for the Lion's share, leaving only the smallest possible morsel for himself.
sentences.zh: 狐狸把几乎全部堆成一大份给狮子，只给自己留下小得不能再小的一点。

sentences.en: "My dear friend," said the Lion, "how did you get the knack of it so well?"
sentences.zh: “好朋友，”狮子说，“你这手怎么练得这么到家？”

sentences.en: The Fox replied, "Me?
sentences.zh: 狐狸答道：“我？

sentences.en: Oh, I took a lesson from the Ass."
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是拿驴当了回先生。”

sentences.en: Happy is he who learns from the misfortunes of others.
sentences.zh: 能从别人的倒霉里学到东西的人，是有福的。

title: The Wolf and the Lamb
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Wolf came upon a Lamb straying from the flock …
sentences.zh: 一只狼撞见一只离了群的小羊……

sentences.en: … and felt some compunction about taking the life of so helpless a creature without some plausible excuse …
sentences.zh: ……它多少有些顾忌：这么个毫无力气的活物，总得找个说得过去的由头才好下手……

sentences.en: … so he cast about for a grievance and said at last, "Last year, sirrah, you grossly insulted me."
sentences.zh: ……于是它搜肠刮肚找了个碴儿，终于开口：“小子，去年你狠狠辱骂过我。”

sentences.en: "That is impossible, sir," bleated the Lamb, "for I wasn't born then."
sentences.zh: “那不可能，先生，”小羊咩咩道，“我那时候还没出生呢。”

sentences.en: "Well," retorted the Wolf, "you feed in my pastures."
sentences.zh: “那好，”狼反驳道，“你在我牧场上吃草。”

sentences.en: "That cannot be," replied the Lamb, "for I have never yet tasted grass."
sentences.zh: “这也不会，”小羊答道，“我至今还没尝过草的滋味。”

sentences.en: "You drink from my spring, then," continued the Wolf.
sentences.zh: “那你喝我泉里的水。”狼又说。

sentences.en: "Indeed, sir," said the poor Lamb, "I have never yet drunk anything but my mother's milk."
sentences.zh: “真的，先生，”可怜的小羊说，“除了母奶，我什么都没喝过。”

sentences.en: "Well, anyhow," said the Wolf, "I'm not going without my dinner": and he sprang upon the Lamb and devoured it without more ado.
sentences.zh: “哼，不管怎样，”狼说，“我可不能空着肚子走。”说着扑上去，不再多话，把小羊吃了。

title: The Fox and the Stork
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Fox invited a Stork to dinner, at which the only fare provided was a large flat dish of soup.
sentences.zh: 狐狸请鹳来吃饭，席上只有一大盘平底的汤。

sentences.en: The Fox lapped it up with great relish, but the Stork with her long bill tried in vain to partake of the savoury broth.
sentences.zh: 狐狸舔得津津有味，鹳却用长嘴试了又试，那鲜汤一点也喝不着。

sentences.en: Her evident distress caused the sly Fox much amusement.
sentences.zh: 她那份窘迫，让狡猾的狐狸看得十分开心。

sentences.en: But not long after the Stork invited him in turn …
sentences.zh: 可没过多久，鹳也回请了他……

sentences.en: … and set before him a pitcher with a long and narrow neck, into which she could get her bill with ease.
sentences.zh: ……端上一只长颈细口的罐子——她的长嘴伸进去毫不费力。

sentences.en: Thus, while she enjoyed her dinner, the Fox sat by hungry and helpless …
sentences.zh: 于是，鹳吃得自在，狐狸却坐在一旁，又饿又没辙……

sentences.en: … for it was impossible for him to reach the tempting contents of the vessel.
sentences.zh: ……罐里那诱人的东西，他怎么也够不着。

title: The Blind Man and the Cub
author: Aesop

sentences.en: There was once a Blind Man who had so fine a sense of touch that …
sentences.zh: 从前有个盲人，触觉极灵敏……

sentences.en: … when any animal was put into his hands, he could tell what it was merely by the feel of it.
sentences.zh: ……无论什么动物放到他手上，他只要摸一摸，就能说出是什么。

sentences.en: One day the Cub of a Wolf was put into his hands, and he was asked what it was.
sentences.zh: 一天，有人把一只狼崽放到他手里，问他这是什么。

sentences.en: He felt it for some time, and then said, "Indeed, I am not sure whether it is a Wolf's Cub or a Fox's …
sentences.zh: 他摸了好一阵，说：“说实话，我拿不准这是狼崽还是狐狸崽……

sentences.en: … but this I know--it would never do to trust it in a sheepfold."
sentences.zh: ……但有一样我清楚——这东西绝不能放进羊圈里。”

sentences.en: Evil tendencies are early shown.
sentences.zh: 恶的苗头，早早就露出来了。

title: The Farmer and His Sons
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Farmer, being at death's door, and desiring to impart to his Sons a secret of much moment, called them round him and said, "My sons, I …
sentences.zh: 一个农夫已到了弥留之际，想把这桩极要紧的秘密交代给儿子们，就把他们叫到跟前，说：“孩子们，我……

sentences.en: … am shortly about to die; I would have you know, therefore, that in my vineyard there lies a hidden treasure.
sentences.zh: ……不久就要去了。所以我要让你们知道：我的葡萄园里埋着一宗财宝。

sentences.en: Dig, and you will find it."
sentences.zh: 挖吧，你们会找到的。”

sentences.en: As soon as their father was dead, the Sons took spade and fork and turned up the soil of the vineyard over and over again, in their …
sentences.zh: 父亲一过世，儿子们就扛起铁锹和耙子，把葡萄园的土翻了一遍又一遍……

sentences.en: … search for the treasure which they supposed to lie buried there.
sentences.zh: ……为的是找那宗他们以为埋在底下的财宝。

sentences.en: They found none, however: but the vines, after so thorough a digging, produced a crop such as had never before been seen.
sentences.zh: 财宝当然没找着；可葡萄藤经这么一通深翻，结出的果子却是从未有过的好收成。

title: The Mouse, the Frog, and the Hawk
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Mouse and a Frog struck up a friendship; they were not well mated …
sentences.zh: 一只老鼠和一只青蛙交上了朋友；这两个实在不般配……

sentences.en: … for the Mouse lived entirely on land, while the Frog was equally at home on land or in the water.
sentences.zh: ……老鼠只住在陆上，青蛙却在水里陆上都自在。

sentences.en: In order that they might never be separated, the Frog tied himself and the Mouse together by the leg with a piece of thread.
sentences.zh: 青蛙为了永不分开，用一根线把自己的腿和老鼠的腿拴在了一起。

sentences.en: As long as they kept on dry land all went fairly well …
sentences.zh: 只要还在干地上，一切倒还顺利……

sentences.en: … but, coming to the edge of a pool, the Frog jumped in, taking the Mouse with him, and began swimming about and croaking with pleasure.
sentences.zh: ……可到了水塘边，青蛙一下跳了进去，把老鼠也带了进去，一边游一边快活地呱呱叫。

sentences.en: The unhappy Mouse, however, was soon drowned, and floated about on the surface in the wake of the Frog.
sentences.zh: 可怜的老鼠很快就淹死了，浮在水面上，被青蛙拖着走。

sentences.en: There he was spied by a Hawk, who pounced down on him and seized him in his talons.
sentences.zh: 一只鹰瞧见了它，俯冲下来，用爪子把它抓住。

sentences.en: The Frog was unable to loose the knot which bound him to the Mouse, and thus was carried off along with him and eaten by the Hawk.
sentences.zh: 青蛙解不开把彼此系在一起的那个结，于是也被一同带走，让鹰吃了。

title: The Boy and the Filberts
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Boy put his hand into a jar of Filberts, and grasped as many as his fist could possibly hold.
sentences.zh: 一个男孩把手伸进装榛子的罐子，一把抓了满满一手。

sentences.en: But when he tried to pull it out again, he found he couldn't do so …
sentences.zh: 可他想把手抽回来时，却怎么也不行……

sentences.en: … for the neck of the jar was too small to allow of the passage of so large a handful.
sentences.zh: ……罐口太窄，那么一大把榛子过不去。

sentences.en: Unwilling to lose his nuts but unable to withdraw his hand, he burst into tears.
sentences.zh: 榛子舍不得丢，手又抽不出，他急得哭了起来。

sentences.en: A bystander, who saw where the trouble lay, said to him, "Come, my boy, don't be so greedy …
sentences.zh: 旁边有人看出了毛病在哪儿，对他说：“好啦，孩子，别这么贪……

sentences.en: … be content with half the amount, and you'll be able to get your hand out without difficulty."
sentences.zh: ……拿一半就够了，手自然就出来了。”

sentences.en: Do not attempt too much at once.
sentences.zh: 一次别想拿太多。

title: The Fox Without a Tail
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A fox once fell into a trap, and after a struggle managed to get free, but with the loss of his brush.
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸掉进陷阱，挣扎一番总算脱了身，尾巴却丢了。

sentences.en: He was then so much ashamed of his appearance that he thought life was not worth living unless he could persuade the other Foxes to part …
sentences.zh: 它觉得自己这副模样实在难看，心想：除非能劝别的狐狸也把尾巴……

sentences.en: … with their tails also, and thus divert attention from his own loss.
sentences.zh: ……都舍掉，把注意力从自己身上引开，否则这日子没法过。

sentences.en: So he called a meeting of all the Foxes, and advised them to cut off their tails …
sentences.zh: 于是它召集了全体狐狸，劝大家把尾巴都割掉……

sentences.en: … "They're ugly things anyhow," he said, "and besides they're heavy, and it's tiresome to be always carrying them about with you."
sentences.zh: 它说：“这东西本来就难看，又沉，整天拖在身上多累赘。”

sentences.en: But one of the other Foxes said, "My friend, if you hadn't lost your own tail, you wouldn't be so keen on getting us to cut off ours."
sentences.zh: 另一只狐狸却说：“朋友，你要是没丢自己的尾巴，才不会这么热心劝我们割呢。”

title: The Blacksmith and His Dog
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Blacksmith had a little Dog, which used to sleep when his master was at work, but was very wide awake indeed when it was time for meals.
sentences.zh: 一个铁匠养了条小狗。主人干活时它就睡觉，一到吃饭的点儿倒是清醒得很。

sentences.en: One day his master pretended to be disgusted at this …
sentences.zh: 有一天，主人装作看不下去的样子……

sentences.en: … and when he had thrown him a bone as usual, he said, "What on earth is the good of a lazy cur like you?
sentences.zh: ……照旧扔给它一根骨头，说：“你这么条懒狗，到底有什么用？

sentences.en: When I am hammering away at my anvil, you just curl up and go to sleep …
sentences.zh: 我在铁砧上叮叮当当干活的时候，你就蜷起来睡大觉……

sentences.en: … but no sooner do I stop for a mouthful of food than you wake up and wag your tail to be fed."
sentences.zh: ……可我只要一停下来吃口东西，你立马就醒，摇着尾巴要吃的。”

sentences.en: Those who will not work deserve to starve.
sentences.zh: 不肯干活的，活该挨饿。

title: The Eagle and His Captor
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Man once caught an Eagle, and after clipping his wings turned him loose among the fowls in his hen-house, where he moped in a corner …
sentences.zh: 有人捉住一只鹰，剪了它的翅膀，把它丢进鸡棚里跟鸡待在一处。它缩在角落里发呆……

sentences.en: … looking very dejected and forlorn.
sentences.zh: ……一副丧气落魄的样子。

sentences.en: After a while his Captor was glad enough to sell him to a neighbour, who took him home and let his wings grow again.
sentences.zh: 过了些日子，捉它的人乐得把它卖给一个邻居；邻居带回家，任它重新长出羽翼。

sentences.en: As soon as he had recovered the use of them, the Eagle flew out and caught a hare, which he brought home and presented to his benefactor.
sentences.zh: 翅膀一能用了，鹰就飞出去抓了一只野兔，带回来送给这位恩人。

sentences.en: A fox observed this, and said to the Eagle, "Don't waste your gifts on him!
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸看在眼里，对鹰说：“别把心思花在他身上！

sentences.en: Go and give them to the man who first caught you …
sentences.zh: 去送给当初捉住你的那个人……

sentences.en: … make him your friend, and then perhaps he won't catch you and clip your wings a second time."
sentences.zh: ……跟他交个朋友，这样他说不定就不会再捉你一次、再剪一次你的翅膀了。”

title: The She-Goats and Their Beards
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Jupiter granted beards to the She-Goats at their own request, much to the disgust of the he-Goats …
sentences.zh: 母山羊们自己请求长胡子，朱庇特就准了。这让公山羊们十分不满……

sentences.en: … who considered this to be an unwarrantable invasion of their rights and dignities.
sentences.zh: ……它们觉得这是对自家权利和体面的无理侵夺。

sentences.en: So they sent a deputation to him to protest against his action.
sentences.zh: 于是它们派了个代表去见朱庇特，抗议这一决定。

sentences.en: He, however, advised them not to raise any objections.
sentences.zh: 朱庇特却劝它们不必反对。

sentences.en: "What's in a tuft of hair?" said he.
sentences.zh: “一撮毛算什么？”他说。

sentences.en: "Let them have it if they want it.
sentences.zh: “她们想要，就让她们留着。

sentences.en: They can never be a match for you in strength."
sentences.zh: 论力气，她们永远比不上你们。”

title: The Shipwrecked Man and the Sea
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Shipwrecked Man cast up on the beach fell asleep after his struggle with the waves.
sentences.zh: 一个遇难的人被浪冲上海滩，跟波涛搏斗了一场，就睡着了。

sentences.en: When he woke up, he bitterly reproached the Sea for its treachery in enticing men with its smooth and smiling surface …
sentences.zh: 醒来后，他痛骂大海阴险：先用平静含笑的水面把人诱来……

sentences.en: … and then, when they were well embarked, turning in fury upon them and sending both ship and sailors to destruction.
sentences.zh: ……等人都上了船，又翻脸发怒，把船和船上的人一并葬送。

sentences.en: The Sea arose in the form of a woman, and replied, "Lay not the blame on me, O sailor, but on the Winds.
sentences.zh: 大海化作一个女子现身，答道：“水手啊，别怪我，去怪风吧。

sentences.en: By nature I am as calm and safe as the land itself …
sentences.zh: 我本性就跟陆地一样平静可靠……

sentences.en: … but the Winds fall upon me with their gusts and gales, and lash me into a fury that is not natural to me."
sentences.zh: ……是风一阵阵扑上来，把我抽打得狂怒——那份狂暴本不是我的性子。”

title: The Lion, the Mouse, and the Fox
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lion was lying asleep at the mouth of his den when a Mouse ran over his back and tickled him so that he woke up with a start and began …
sentences.zh: 一头狮子在洞口睡觉，一只老鼠从它背上跑过，挠得它猛地惊醒……

sentences.en: … looking about everywhere to see what it was that had disturbed him.
sentences.zh: ……四下张望，想弄清是什么惊了它。

sentences.en: A Fox, who was looking on, thought he would have a joke at the expense of the Lion …
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸在旁看着，想着拿狮子开个玩笑……

sentences.en: … so he said, "Well, this is the first time I've seen a Lion afraid of a Mouse."
sentences.zh: ……就说：“哟，我这还是头一回见狮子怕老鼠。”

sentences.en: "Afraid of a Mouse?" said the Lion testily: "not I!
sentences.zh: “怕老鼠？”狮子没好气地说，“我才不怕！

sentences.en: It's his bad manners I can't stand."
sentences.zh: 我受不了的是它不懂规矩。”

title: The Two Frogs
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Two Frogs were neighbours.
sentences.zh: 两只青蛙是邻居。

sentences.en: One lived in a marsh, where there was plenty of water, which frogs love …
sentences.zh: 一只住在沼泽里，那儿水多，正是青蛙喜欢的地方……

sentences.en: … the other in a lane some distance away, where all the water to be had was that which lay in the ruts after rain.
sentences.zh: ……另一只住在远处一条小路上，那儿唯一的水，就是雨后积在车辙里的那点。

sentences.en: The Marsh Frog warned his friend and pressed him to come and live with him in the marsh …
sentences.zh: 住沼泽的青蛙劝告朋友，力邀它搬来同住……

sentences.en: … for he would find his quarters there far more comfortable and--what was still more important--more safe.
sentences.zh: ……说这儿住着舒服得多，更要紧的是也安全得多。

sentences.en: But the other refused, saying that he could not bring himself to move from a place to which he had become accustomed.
sentences.zh: 可另一只不肯，说自己实在舍不得离开住惯了的地方。

sentences.en: A few days afterwards a heavy waggon came down the lane, and he was crushed to death under the wheels.
sentences.zh: 没过几天，一辆大车从那条小路碾过，它就被车轮压死了。

title: The Mouse and the Bull
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Bull gave chase to a Mouse which had bitten him in the nose: but the Mouse was too quick for him and slipped into a hole in a wall.
sentences.zh: 一只老鼠咬了公牛的鼻子，公牛追它；可老鼠比它灵巧，一钻就进了墙洞。

sentences.en: The Bull charged furiously into the wall again and again until he was tired out, and sank down on the ground exhausted with his efforts.
sentences.zh: 公牛一次次狠命往墙上撞，直到累得瘫倒在地。

sentences.en: When all was quiet, the Mouse darted out and bit him again.
sentences.zh: 等四下安静了，老鼠蹿出来又咬它一口。

sentences.en: Beside himself with rage he started to his feet, but by that time the Mouse was back in his hole again …
sentences.zh: 公牛气得发狂，猛地站起来，可老鼠早已又缩回洞里……

sentences.en: … and he could do nothing but bellow and fume in helpless anger.
sentences.zh: ……它只能干吼、干生气，一点办法也没有。

sentences.en: Presently he heard a shrill little voice say from inside the wall, "You big fellows don't always have it your own way, you see …
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，墙里传出一个尖细的声音：“你看，你们大块头也不是总能随心所欲……

sentences.en: … sometimes we little ones come off best."
sentences.zh: ……有时候我们小家伙反倒占上风。”

sentences.en: The battle is not always to the strong.
sentences.zh: 得胜的，未必总是强者。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Stag with One Eye
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Stag, blind of one eye, was grazing close to the sea-shore and kept his sound eye turned towards the land …
sentences.zh: 一头瞎了一只眼的雄鹿在海边吃草，把好的那只眼始终朝着陆地……

sentences.en: … so as to be able to perceive the approach of the hounds …
sentences.zh: ……好察觉猎犬的动静……

sentences.en: … while the blind eye he turned towards the sea, never suspecting that any danger would threaten him from that quarter.
sentences.zh: ……瞎的那只则对着海，它从没想到危险会从那边来。

sentences.en: As it fell out, however, some sailors, coasting along the shore, spied him and shot an arrow at him, by which he was mortally wounded.
sentences.zh: 可事情偏偏如此：几个水手沿岸航行，瞧见了它，一箭射来，正中要害。

sentences.en: As he lay dying, he said to himself, "Wretch that I am!
sentences.zh: 临死时它自言自语：“我真是糊涂！

sentences.en: I bethought me of the dangers of the land, whence none assailed me: but I feared no peril from the sea, yet thence has come my ruin."
sentences.zh: 我提防着陆上的危险，陆上却什么也没来；我不曾怕过海，偏是海要了我的命。”

sentences.en: Misfortune often assails us from an unexpected quarter.
sentences.zh: 祸患常从意想不到的地方来。

title: The Wolf and the Shepherd
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Wolf hung about near a flock of sheep for a long time, but made no attempt to molest them.
sentences.zh: 一只狼在羊群附近转了很久，却始终没去动它们。

sentences.en: The Shepherd at first kept a sharp eye on him, for he naturally thought he meant mischief …
sentences.zh: 牧人起初盯得很紧，因为他自然认为这狼没安好心……

sentences.en: … but as time went by and the Wolf showed no inclination to meddle with the flock, he began to look upon him more as a protector than as …
sentences.zh: ……可日子一长，见狼并没有要碰羊群的意思，他便渐渐把它看作守护者，而不是……

sentences.en: … an enemy: and when one day some errand took him to the city, he felt no uneasiness at leaving the Wolf with the sheep.
sentences.zh: ……敌人了。有一天他进城办事，把狼和羊留在一处，也毫不担心。

sentences.en: But as soon as his back was turned the Wolf attacked them and killed the greater number.
sentences.zh: 可他前脚刚走，狼就扑向羊群，把大半的羊都咬死了。

sentences.en: When the Shepherd returned and saw the havoc he had wrought, he cried, "It serves me right for trusting my flock to a Wolf."
sentences.zh: 牧人回来，看见这一片惨状，叫道：“把羊托给狼，我这是活该。”

title: The Ass, the Cock, and the Lion
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Ass and a Cock were in a cattle-pen together.
sentences.zh: 一头驴和一只公鸡同在一个牲畜栏里。

sentences.en: Presently a Lion, who had been starving for days, came along and was just about to fall upon the Ass and make a meal of him when the …
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，一头饿了几天肚子的狮子走来，正要扑向驴饱餐一顿，那……

sentences.en: … Cock, rising to his full height and flapping his wings vigorously, uttered a tremendous crow.
sentences.zh: ……公鸡却挺身站直，使劲扑扇翅膀，发出一声响亮的啼鸣。

sentences.en: Now, if there is one thing that frightens a Lion, it is the crowing of a Cock: and this one had no sooner heard the noise than he fled.
sentences.zh: 要说有一样东西能让狮子害怕，那就是公鸡打鸣。这头狮子一听见，转身就逃。

sentences.en: The Ass was mightily elated at this, and thought that, if the Lion couldn't face a Cock, he would be still less likely to stand up to an …
sentences.zh: 驴得意极了，心想：狮子连公鸡都不敢对付，就更不敢跟一头……

sentences.en: … Ass: so he ran out and pursued him.
sentences.zh: ……驴较量了。于是它冲出去追赶狮子。

sentences.en: But when the two had got well out of sight and hearing of the Cock, the Lion suddenly turned upon the Ass and ate him up.
sentences.zh: 可等两者都跑得看不见公鸡、也听不见鸡叫了，狮子突然回过头来，把驴吃掉了。

sentences.en: False confidence often leads to disaster.
sentences.zh: 错估自己，常常招来灾祸。

title: The Lion and the Bull
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lion saw a fine fat Bull pasturing among a herd of cattle and cast about for some means of getting him into his clutches …
sentences.zh: 一头狮子看见牛群里有一头肥壮的公牛在吃草，便盘算着怎么把它弄到手……

sentences.en: … so he sent him word that he was sacrificing a sheep, and asked if he would do him the honour of dining with him.
sentences.zh: ……于是它捎话过去，说自己正宰一只羊，问公牛肯不肯赏光来共进晚餐。

sentences.en: The Bull accepted the invitation, but, on arriving at the Lion's den, he saw a great array of saucepans and spits …
sentences.zh: 公牛应了邀，可到了狮子的洞口，只见摆着大堆的锅和烤肉叉……

sentences.en: … but no sign of a sheep; so he turned on his heel and walked quietly away.
sentences.zh: ……却不见半只羊的影子。它转身就走，一声不响。

sentences.en: The Lion called after him in an injured tone to ask the reason, and the Bull turned round and said, "I have reason enough.
sentences.zh: 狮子在背后委屈地叫住它问缘由，公牛回头说：“理由足够了。

sentences.en: When I saw all your preparations it struck me at once that the victim was to be a Bull and not a sheep."
sentences.zh: 我一见你这番准备就明白了：要当祭品的是一头公牛，不是一只羊。”

sentences.en: The net is spread in vain in sight of the bird.
sentences.zh: 网当着鸟的面撒下，是白撒。
