title: The Cat and the Mice
author: Aesop

sentences.en: There was once a house that was overrun with Mice.
sentences.zh: 从前有一所房子，老鼠成群，闹得厉害。

sentences.en: A Cat heard of this, and said to herself, "That's the place for me," and off she went and took up her quarters in the house …
sentences.zh: 一只猫听说此事，自言自语道：「那正是我该去的地方。」于是她就去了，在那所房子里安顿下来……

sentences.en: … and caught the Mice one by one and ate them.
sentences.zh: ……把老鼠一只一只抓住吃掉。

sentences.en: At last the Mice could stand it no longer, and they determined to take to their holes and stay there.
sentences.zh: 到最后老鼠们再也受不了了，决定钻进洞里不再出来。

sentences.en: "That's awkward," said the Cat to herself: "the only thing to do is to coax them out by a trick."
sentences.zh: 「这就难办了，」猫自言自语，「唯一的办法是用计策把它们引出来。」

sentences.en: So she considered a while, and then climbed up the wall and let herself hang down by her hind legs from a peg, and pretended to be dead.
sentences.zh: 她想了一会儿，然后爬上墙，用后腿挂在一根木钉上倒吊着，装死。

sentences.en: By and by a Mouse peeped out and saw the Cat hanging there.
sentences.zh: 不久，一只老鼠探出头来，看见猫吊在那里。

sentences.en: "Aha!" it cried, "you're very clever, madam, no doubt …
sentences.zh: 「啊哈！」它叫道，「夫人，您确实很聪明……」

sentences.en: … but you may turn yourself into a bag of meal hanging there, if you like, yet you won't catch us coming anywhere near you."
sentences.zh: 「……可是就算您愿意把自己变成一袋面粉挂在那儿，也休想让我们靠近你一步。」

sentences.en: If you are wise you won't be deceived by the innocent airs of those whom you have once found to be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 聪明人不会被那些一旦被识破危险就装出无辜模样的家伙骗到。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Mice in Council
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Once upon a time all the Mice met together in Council, and discussed the best means of securing themselves against the attacks of the cat.
sentences.zh: 有一次，所有的老鼠聚在一起开会，讨论用什么办法最好，能保自己不受猫的袭击。

sentences.en: After several suggestions had been debated, a Mouse of some standing and experience got up and said, "I think I have hit upon a plan …
sentences.zh: 议论过几个提议之后，一只颇有地位和经验的老鼠站起来说：「我想出了一个办法……」

sentences.en: … which will ensure our safety in the future, provided you approve and carry it out.
sentences.zh: 「……只要你们赞成并照办，就能保证我们今后的安全。」

sentences.en: It is that we should fasten a bell round the neck of our enemy the cat, which will by its tinkling warn us of her approach."
sentences.zh: 「那就是在我们的敌人猫的脖子上系一只铃铛，铃声一响就能提醒我们她来了。」

sentences.en: This proposal was warmly applauded, and it had been already decided to adopt it …
sentences.zh: 这个提议受到热烈鼓掌，大家已经决定采纳……

sentences.en: … when an old Mouse got upon his feet and said, "I agree with you all that the plan before us is an admirable one …
sentences.zh: ……这时一只年迈的老鼠站起来说：「我同意各位的看法，眼前这个计策确实妙……」

sentences.en: … but may I ask who is going to bell the cat?"
sentences.zh: 「……可是我想请教一句：谁去给猫系铃铛呢？」

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Old Woman and the Doctor
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Old Woman became almost totally blind from a disease of the eyes, and, after consulting a Doctor, made an agreement with him in the …
sentences.zh: 一位老妇因眼疾几乎完全失明。她请教过一位医生后，当着见证人的面与他立下约定：

sentences.en: … presence of witnesses that she should pay him a high fee if he cured her, while if he failed he was to receive nothing.
sentences.zh: ……若治好，她付他一笔丰厚的酬金；若治不好，他分文不取。

sentences.en: The Doctor accordingly prescribed a course of treatment …
sentences.zh: 医生于是开了一套疗程……

sentences.en: … and every time he paid her a visit he took away with him some article out of the house, until at last …
sentences.zh: ……而他每次上门出诊，都会顺手从她家里带走一件东西，直到最后……

sentences.en: … when he visited her for the last time, and the cure was complete, there was nothing left.
sentences.zh: ……当他最后一次来看诊、疗程完成时，家里已经什么都剩不下了。

sentences.en: When the Old Woman saw that the house was empty she refused to pay him his fee …
sentences.zh: 老妇见屋里空了，便拒付酬金……

sentences.en: … and, after repeated refusals on her part, he sued her before the magistrates for payment of her debt.
sentences.zh: ……她一再拒绝之后，医生便到地方官那里告她，索讨这笔欠款。

sentences.en: On being brought into court she was ready with her defence.
sentences.zh: 被带上公堂时，她早有辩解。

sentences.en: "The claimant," said she, "has stated the facts about our agreement correctly.
sentences.zh: 「原告，」她说，「把我们之间的约定讲得没错。

sentences.en: I undertook to pay him a fee if he cured me, and he, on his part, promised to charge nothing if he failed.
sentences.zh: 我承诺若治好便付酬金，而他那边则答应若治不好就不收分文。

sentences.en: Now, he says I am cured; but I say that I am blinder than ever, and I can prove what I say.
sentences.zh: 现在他说我治好了；可我说我比从前更瞎，而且我能证明我说的话。

sentences.en: When my eyes were bad I could at any rate see well enough to be aware that my house contained a certain amount of furniture and other …
sentences.zh: 我眼睛不好的时候，至少还能看清我家里有多少家具和别的……

sentences.en: … things; but now, when according to him I am cured, I am entirely unable to see anything there at all."
sentences.zh: 「……东西；可是如今，按他的说法我已痊愈，我却完全看不见家里有任何东西了。」

title: The Ass, the Fox, and the Lion
author: Aesop

sentences.en: An Ass and a Fox went into partnership and sallied out to forage for food together.
sentences.zh: 一头驴和一只狐狸结成了搭伴，一起出去觅食。

sentences.en: They hadn't gone far before they saw a Lion coming their way, at which they were both dreadfully frightened.
sentences.zh: 没走多远，它们就看见一头狮子朝这边来，两个都吓坏了。

sentences.en: But the Fox thought he saw a way of saving his own skin …
sentences.zh: 可是狐狸觉得自己看到了一条保住性命的办法……

sentences.en: … and went boldly up to the Lion and whispered in his ear, "I'll manage that you shall get hold of the Ass without the trouble of …
sentences.zh: ……便壮着胆子走到狮子跟前，在他耳边低声说：「我能让您不必费事就抓住那头驴……」

sentences.en: … stalking him, if you'll promise to let me go free."
sentences.zh: 「……免去跟踪的麻烦，只要您答应放我一条生路。」

sentences.en: The Lion agreed to this, and the Fox then rejoined his companion and contrived before long to lead him by a hidden pit …
sentences.zh: 狮子答应了。狐狸于是回到伙伴身边，没多久就设法把它引到一个隐着的深坑旁……

sentences.en: … which some hunter had dug as a trap for wild animals, and into which he fell.
sentences.zh: ……那坑是哪个猎人挖来捕野兽的陷阱，驴掉了进去。

sentences.en: When the Lion saw that the Ass was safely caught and couldn't get away, it was to the Fox that he first turned his attention …
sentences.zh: 狮子见驴已被牢牢困住逃不掉了，便先转过头来对付狐狸……

sentences.en: … and he soon finished him off, and then at his leisure proceeded to feast upon the Ass.
sentences.zh: ……很快就结果了他，然后才不慌不忙地饱餐那头驴。

sentences.en: Betray a friend, and you'll often find you have ruined yourself.
sentences.zh: 背叛朋友的人，往往发现毁掉的是自己。

title: The North Wind and the Sun
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A dispute arose between the North Wind and the Sun, each claiming that he was stronger than the other.
sentences.zh: 北风与太阳争执起来，双方都声称自己比对方强。

sentences.en: At last they agreed to try their powers upon a traveller, to see which could soonest strip him of his cloak.
sentences.zh: 最后他们约定在一个行人身上试本事，看谁先让他脱下斗篷。

sentences.en: The North Wind had the first try; and, gathering up all his force for the attack, he came whirling furiously down upon the man …
sentences.zh: 北风先试；他聚起全身力气发起攻势，猛烈地旋转着向那人扑下去……

sentences.en: … and caught up his cloak as though he would wrest it from him by one single effort …
sentences.zh: ……一把揪住他的斗篷，仿佛要一举把它扯下来……

sentences.en: … but the harder he blew, the more closely the man wrapped it round himself.
sentences.zh: ……可他吹得越猛，那人把斗篷裹得越紧。

sentences.en: Then came the turn of the Sun.
sentences.zh: 然后轮到太阳了。

sentences.en: At first he beamed gently upon the traveller, who soon unclasped his cloak and walked on with it hanging loosely about his shoulders …
sentences.zh: 起初他只是温和地照着那行人，那人很快便解开斗篷，任它松松地搭在肩上继续走……

sentences.en: … then he shone forth in his full strength …
sentences.zh: ……接着他放出全部热力……

sentences.en: … and the man, before he had gone many steps, was glad to throw his cloak right off and complete his journey more lightly clad.
sentences.zh: ……那人没走几步，就乐意地把斗篷彻底脱掉，穿着轻便地走完了旅程。

sentences.en: Persuasion is better than force
sentences.zh: 说服胜于强迫。

title: The Mistress and Her Servants
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Widow, thrifty and industrious, had two servants, whom she kept pretty hard at work.
sentences.zh: 一位勤俭的寡妇有两个仆人，她叫他们干活干得相当辛苦。

sentences.en: They were not allowed to lie long abed in the mornings, but the old lady had them up and doing as soon as the cock crew.
sentences.zh: 早上不许他们赖床太久，公鸡一叫，老太太就让他们起来干活。

sentences.en: They disliked intensely having to get up at such an hour, especially in winter-time …
sentences.zh: 他们极不愿在那个时辰起床，尤其冬天……

sentences.en: … and they thought that if it were not for the cock waking up their Mistress so horribly early, they could sleep longer.
sentences.zh: ……他们想，要不是公鸡那么早把主妇叫醒，自己就能多睡一会儿。

sentences.en: So they caught it and wrung its neck.
sentences.zh: 于是他们抓住公鸡，拧断了它的脖子。

sentences.en: But they weren't prepared for the consequences.
sentences.zh: 可他们没料到后果。

sentences.en: For what happened was that their Mistress, not hearing the cock crow as usual, waked them up earlier than ever …
sentences.zh: 结果主妇听不到公鸡照常打鸣，反而比从前更早把他们叫醒了……

sentences.en: … and set them to work in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: ……让他们半夜里就起来干活。

title: The Lion and the Mouse
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lion asleep in his lair was waked up by a Mouse running over his face.
sentences.zh: 一只狮子在洞穴里睡觉，被一只从脸上跑过的老鼠弄醒了。

sentences.en: Losing his temper he seized it with his paw and was about to kill it.
sentences.zh: 他动了怒，用爪子抓住它，正要弄死它。

sentences.en: The Mouse, terrified, piteously entreated him to spare its life.
sentences.zh: 老鼠吓得要命，可怜巴巴地哀求他饶自己一命。

sentences.en: "Please let me go," it cried, "and one day I will repay you for your kindness."
sentences.zh: 「请放我走吧，」它叫道，「总有一天我会报答您的恩情。」

sentences.en: The idea of so insignificant a creature ever being able to do anything for him amused the Lion so much that he laughed aloud …
sentences.zh: 想到这么一个微不足道的小东西居然能帮上自己的忙，狮子觉得十分可笑，竟笑出声来……

sentences.en: … and good-humouredly let it go.
sentences.zh: ……便好脾气地把它放了。

sentences.en: But the Mouse's chance came, after all.
sentences.zh: 可老鼠的机会终究还是来了。

sentences.en: One day the Lion got entangled in a net which had been spread for game by some hunters …
sentences.zh: 有一天，狮子被几个猎人张设捕猎的网缠住了……

sentences.en: … and the Mouse heard and recognised his roars of anger and ran to the spot.
sentences.zh: ……老鼠听见并认出了他愤怒的吼声，便跑到那里。

sentences.en: Without more ado it set to work to gnaw the ropes with its teeth, and succeeded before long in setting the Lion free.
sentences.zh: 它二话不说就用牙咬那些绳子，没多久便把狮子放开。

sentences.en: "There!" said the Mouse, "you laughed at me when I promised I would repay you: but now you see, even a Mouse can help a Lion."
sentences.zh: 「您看！」老鼠说，「我答应报答您的时候，您还笑我；可如今您看到了，就连一只老鼠也能帮上狮子的忙。」

title: The Crow and the Pitcher
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A thirsty Crow found a Pitcher with some water in it …
sentences.zh: 一只口渴的乌鸦找到一只水罐，里面有些水……

sentences.en: … but so little was there that, try as she might, she could not reach it with her beak …
sentences.zh: ……可水太少，她怎么试，嘴也够不到……

sentences.en: … and it seemed as though she would die of thirst within sight of the remedy.
sentences.zh: ……眼看解渴的东西就在眼前，她却像是要渴死了。

sentences.en: At last she hit upon a clever plan.
sentences.zh: 最后她想到一个巧办法。

sentences.en: She began dropping pebbles into the Pitcher, and with each pebble the water rose a little higher until at last it reached the brim …
sentences.zh: 她开始往罐里丢小石子，每丢一颗，水就升高一点，直到最后升到罐口……

sentences.en: … and the knowing bird was enabled to quench her thirst.
sentences.zh: ……这只聪明的鸟便得以解了渴。

sentences.en: Necessity is the mother of invention.
sentences.zh: 需要是发明之母。

title: The Hares and the Frogs
author: Aesop

sentences.en: The Hares once gathered together and lamented the unhappiness of their lot, exposed as they were to dangers on all sides and lacking the …
sentences.zh: 野兔们曾聚在一起哀叹自己命苦：它们四面受敌，又缺少……

sentences.en: … strength and the courage to hold their own.
sentences.zh: ……保护自己的力气和勇气。

sentences.en: Men, dogs, birds and beasts of prey were all their enemies, and killed and devoured them daily …
sentences.zh: 人、狗、鸟和猛兽都是它们的敌人，天天捕杀吞食它们……

sentences.en: … and sooner than endure such persecution any longer, they one and all determined to end their miserable lives.
sentences.zh: ……它们再不愿忍受这样的迫害，便一致决定结束这悲惨的性命。

sentences.en: Thus resolved and desperate, they rushed in a body towards a neighbouring pool, intending to drown themselves.
sentences.zh: 既下了这样的决心，它们便绝望地成群奔向附近一个水塘，打算投水自尽。

sentences.en: On the bank were sitting a number of Frogs, who …
sentences.zh: 岸上坐着一群青蛙，它们……

sentences.en: … when they heard the noise of the Hares as they ran, with one accord leaped into the water and hid themselves in the depths.
sentences.zh: ……听见野兔奔跑的声响，便一齐跳进水里，躲到深处去了。

sentences.en: Then one of the older Hares who was wiser than the rest cried out to his companions, "Stop, my friends, take heart …
sentences.zh: 这时，一只比同伴们都聪明的年长野兔向大伙喊道：「停下吧，朋友们，振作起来……」

sentences.en: … don't let us destroy ourselves after all …
sentences.zh: 「……我们终究不必自寻短见……」

sentences.en: … see, here are creatures who are afraid of us, and who must, therefore, be still more timid than ourselves."
sentences.zh: 「……看，这里有怕我们的生灵，可见它们必定比我们更胆小。」

title: The Goods and the Ills
author: Aesop

sentences.en: There was a time in the youth of the world when Goods and Ills entered equally into the concerns of men …
sentences.zh: 在世界初生的年月，善与恶同等地参与人间的事务……

sentences.en: … so that the Goods did not prevail to make them altogether blessed, nor the Ills to make them wholly miserable.
sentences.zh: ……因此善不足以使人全然有福，恶也不至于使人彻底不幸。

sentences.en: But owing to the foolishness of mankind the Ills multiplied greatly in number and increased in strength, until it seemed as though they …
sentences.zh: 可是由于人类的愚昧，恶的数目大增、势力渐强，看来它们……

sentences.en: … would deprive the Goods of all share in human affairs, and banish them from the earth.
sentences.zh: ……就要剥夺善在人间的一切份位，把它们逐出大地。

sentences.en: The latter, therefore, betook themselves to heaven and complained to Jupiter of the treatment they had received, at the same time praying …
sentences.zh: 于是善便上到天界，向朱庇特诉说所受的待遇，同时祈求……

sentences.en: … him to grant them protection from the Ills, and to advise them concerning the manner of their intercourse with men.
sentences.zh: ……他赐予保护，使它们不受害于恶，并就它们与人类往来的方式给予指点。

sentences.en: Jupiter granted their request for protection, and decreed that for the future they should not go among men openly in a body …
sentences.zh: 朱庇特应允了它们求护的请求，并规定今后它们不得成群显形地进入人间……

sentences.en: … and so be liable to attack from the hostile Ills, but singly and unobserved, and at infrequent and unexpected intervals.
sentences.zh: ……以免遭到恶的攻击，而要单个地、不为人察觉地前往，且次数稀少、时机难料。

sentences.en: Hence it is that the earth is full of Ills, for they come and go as they please and are never far away …
sentences.zh: 因此大地上满是恶，因为它们来去自如，从不远离……

sentences.en: … while Goods, alas! come one by one only, and have to travel all the way from heaven, so that they are very seldom seen.
sentences.zh: ……而善呢，唉！只能一个一个地来，还要从天上一路跋涉，所以极少为人所见。

title: The Milkmaid and Her Pail
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A farmer's daughter had been out to milk the cows, and was returning to the dairy carrying her pail of milk upon her head.
sentences.zh: 农家的女儿出去挤了牛奶，正头顶着奶桶回奶房去。

sentences.en: As she walked along, she fell a-musing after this fashion …
sentences.zh: 走着走着，她便这样出起神来……

sentences.en: … "The milk in this pail will provide me with cream, which I will make into butter and take to market to sell.
sentences.zh: 「这桶奶能给我提出奶油，我要把它做成黄油，拿到集市上去卖。

sentences.en: With the money I will buy a number of eggs, and these, when hatched, will produce chickens …
sentences.zh: 得了钱我就买些鸡蛋，蛋孵出来就是小鸡……

sentences.en: … and by and by I shall have quite a large poultry-yard.
sentences.zh: ……不久我就能有一大片养鸡场了。

sentences.en: Then I shall sell some of my fowls, and with the money which they will bring in I will buy myself a new gown …
sentences.zh: 然后我卖掉几只鸡，用换来的钱给自己买一件新长裙……

sentences.en: … which I shall wear when I go to the fair …
sentences.zh: ……赶集的时候就穿上它……

sentences.en: … and all the young fellows will admire it, and come and make love to me, but I shall toss my head and have nothing to say to them."
sentences.zh: ……所有的小伙子都会称赞它，来向我献殷勤，可我只把头一甩，理也不理他们。」

sentences.en: Forgetting all about the pail, and suiting the action to the word, she tossed her head.
sentences.zh: 她全然忘了头上的奶桶，说到做到，真把头一甩。

sentences.en: Down went the pail, all the milk was spilled, and all her fine castles in the air vanished in a moment!
sentences.zh: 奶桶摔了下来，奶全洒了，她那些空中楼阁也一下子没了踪影！

sentences.en: Do not count your chickens before they are hatched.
sentences.zh: 鸡蛋还没孵出来，别先数小鸡。

title: The Fox and the Monkey
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Fox and a Monkey were on the road together, and fell into a dispute as to which of the two was the better born.
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸和一只猴子同行，为了谁出身更高贵而争了起来。

sentences.en: They kept it up for some time, till they came to a place where the road passed through a cemetery full of monuments …
sentences.zh: 他们争了好一阵，直到走到一处，路从满是墓碑的墓地中穿过……

sentences.en: … when the Monkey stopped and looked about him and gave a great sigh.
sentences.zh: ……猴子停了下来，四下张望，重重叹了口气。

sentences.en: "Why do you sigh?" said the Fox.
sentences.zh: 「你叹什么气？」狐狸说。

sentences.en: The Monkey pointed to the tombs and replied, "All the monuments that you see here were put up in honour of my forefathers …
sentences.zh: 猴子指着那些坟说：「你看见的这些碑，都是为了纪念我的祖先而立……」

sentences.en: … who in their day were eminent men."
sentences.zh: 「……他们当年都是显赫的人物。」

sentences.en: The Fox was speechless for a moment, but quickly recovering he said, "Oh! don't stop at any lie, sir …
sentences.zh: 狐狸一时说不出话，但很快缓过神来，说：「哦！先生，尽管往下编，别停下……」

sentences.en: … you're quite safe: I'm sure none of your ancestors will rise up and expose you."
sentences.zh: 「……您很安全：我敢说您的祖先没有一个会爬起来揭穿您。」

sentences.en: Boasters brag most when they cannot be detected.
sentences.zh: 吹牛的人，在无人能揭穿他时吹得最凶。

title: The Bear and the Travellers
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Two Travellers were on the road together, when a Bear suddenly appeared on the scene.
sentences.zh: 两个旅人同行，忽然一头熊出现在眼前。

sentences.en: Before he observed them, one made for a tree at the side of the road, and climbed up into the branches and hid there.
sentences.zh: 还没等熊看见他们，其中一个就奔向路旁的树，爬上枝头躲了起来。

sentences.en: The other was not so nimble as his companion; and, as he could not escape, he threw himself on the ground and pretended to be dead.
sentences.zh: 另一个不如同伴灵巧，逃不掉了，便扑倒在地装死。

sentences.en: The Bear came up and sniffed all round him, but he kept perfectly still and held his breath …
sentences.zh: 熊走过来，在他周身嗅了又嗅，而他一动不动，屏住呼吸……

sentences.en: … for they say that a bear will not touch a dead body.
sentences.zh: ……因为据说熊不碰死尸。

sentences.en: The Bear took him for a corpse, and went away.
sentences.zh: 熊当他是个死人，便走开了。

sentences.en: When the coast was clear, the Traveller in the tree came down …
sentences.zh: 危险过去后，树上的旅人爬了下来……

sentences.en: … and asked the other what it was the Bear had whispered to him when he put his mouth to his ear.
sentences.zh: ……问另一个人，熊把嘴凑到他耳边时说了什么悄悄话。

sentences.en: The other replied, "He told me never again to travel with a friend who deserts you at the first sign of danger."
sentences.zh: 那人答道：「它告诉我，以后别再和那种一有危险就先逃走的朋友同行。」

sentences.en: Misfortune tests the sincerity of friendship.
sentences.zh: 患难见真情。

title: The Ass and the Lap-dog
author: Aesop

sentences.en: There was once a man who had an Ass and a Lap-dog.
sentences.zh: 从前有个人，养着一头驴和一只哈巴狗。

sentences.en: The Ass was housed in the stable with plenty of oats and hay to eat and was as well off as an ass could be.
sentences.zh: 驴住在马厩里，有充足的燕麦和干草吃，日子过得再舒坦不过。

sentences.en: The little Dog was made a great pet of by his master, who fondled him and often let him lie in his lap …
sentences.zh: 那只小狗却被主人当成宝贝，主人爱抚它，常让它卧在膝上……

sentences.en: … and if he went out to dinner, he would bring back a tit-bit or two to give him when he ran to meet him on his return.
sentences.zh: ……主人外出赴宴，回来时小狗跑去迎接，他总会带回一两口好吃的东西给它。

sentences.en: The Ass had, it is true, a good deal of work to do, carting or grinding the corn, or carrying the burdens of the farm …
sentences.zh: 驴确实有不少活要干：拉车、磨谷，或者驮运农场的重物……

sentences.en: … and ere long he became very jealous, contrasting his own life of labour with the ease and idleness of the Lap-dog.
sentences.zh: ……不久它就十分嫉妒起来，拿自己劳苦的日子对比哈巴狗的安逸闲散。

sentences.en: At last one day he broke his halter, and frisking into the house just as his master sat down to dinner, he pranced and capered about …
sentences.zh: 终于有一天它挣断了缰绳，正当主人坐下吃饭时欢跳着冲进屋里，蹦来跳去……

sentences.en: … mimicking the frolics of the little favourite, upsetting the table and smashing the crockery with his clumsy efforts.
sentences.zh: ……模仿那小宠物的嬉闹，笨手笨脚地撞翻了桌子，把碗碟砸得粉碎。

sentences.en: Not content with that, he even tried to jump on his master's lap, as he had so often seen the dog allowed to do.
sentences.zh: 它还不满足，甚至想跳到主人膝上去——它常看见狗被允许这样。

sentences.en: At that the servants, seeing the danger their master was in, belaboured the silly Ass with sticks and cudgels …
sentences.zh: 这时仆人们见主人有危险，便用棍棒狠打这头蠢驴……

sentences.en: … and drove him back to his stable half dead with his beating.
sentences.zh: ……把它打得半死，赶回了马厩。

sentences.en: "Alas!" he cried, "all this I have brought on myself.
sentences.zh: 「唉！」它叫道，「这都是我自找的。

sentences.en: Why could I not be satisfied with my natural and honourable position, without wishing to imitate the ridiculous antics of that useless …
sentences.zh: 我为什么不安守自己本分而体面的位置，偏要去学那没用的……

sentences.en: … little Lap-dog?"
sentences.zh: 「……小哈巴狗的滑稽把戏呢？」

title: The Shepherd's Boy and the Wolf
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Shepherd's Boy was tending his flock near a village …
sentences.zh: 一个牧童在村子附近放羊……

sentences.en: … and thought it would be great fun to hoax the villagers by pretending that a Wolf was attacking the sheep …
sentences.zh: ……他觉得假装有狼来袭击羊群、骗骗村里人一定很好玩……

sentences.en: … so he shouted out, "Wolf! wolf!" and when the people came running up he laughed at them for their pains.
sentences.zh: ……于是大喊「狼来了！狼来了！」等人们跑来，他又笑人家白忙一场。

sentences.en: He did this more than once, and every time the villagers found they had been hoaxed, for there was no Wolf at all.
sentences.zh: 他这样干了好几次，每次村民都发现自己被骗了，根本没有狼。

sentences.en: At last a Wolf really did come, and the Boy cried, "Wolf! wolf!" as loud as he could …
sentences.zh: 后来狼真的来了，牧童拼命大喊「狼来了！狼来了！」……

sentences.en: … but the people were so used to hearing him call that they took no notice of his cries for help.
sentences.zh: ……可人们听惯了他的喊叫，对他的求救毫不理会。

sentences.en: And so the Wolf had it all his own way, and killed off sheep after sheep at his leisure.
sentences.zh: 于是狼为所欲为，不慌不忙地把羊一只只咬死。

sentences.en: You cannot believe a liar even when he tells the truth.
sentences.zh: 爱说谎的人，即使说真话也没人信。

title: The Bee and Jupiter
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Queen Bee from Hymettus flew up to Olympus with some fresh honey from the hive as a present to Jupiter …
sentences.zh: 一只来自许墨托斯的蜂后飞到奥林匹斯山，带着蜂巢里新鲜的蜜献给朱庇特……

sentences.en: … who was so pleased with the gift that he promised to give her anything she liked to ask for.
sentences.zh: ……朱庇特很喜欢这份礼物，便答应给她任何她想要的东西。

sentences.en: She said she would be very grateful if he would give stings to the bees, to kill people who robbed them of their honey.
sentences.zh: 她说，若他赐给蜜蜂毒刺，好刺死那些偷蜜的人，她将感激不尽。

sentences.en: Jupiter was greatly displeased with this request, for he loved mankind …
sentences.zh: 朱庇特对这个请求很不高兴，因为他爱护人类……

sentences.en: … but he had given his word, so he said that stings they should have.
sentences.zh: ……但他已许下诺言，便说既如此就赐它们刺。

sentences.en: The stings he gave them, however, were of such a kind that whenever a bee stings a man the sting is left in the wound and the bee dies.
sentences.zh: 然而他给的刺是这样的：蜂一刺人，刺便留在伤口里，而蜂自己也会死去。

sentences.en: Evil wishes, like fowls, come home to roost.
sentences.zh: 恶愿如鸡，终归自家栖处。

title: The Ass and His Burdens
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Pedlar who owned an Ass one day bought a quantity of salt, and loaded up his beast with as much as he could bear.
sentences.zh: 一个货郎有一头驴。有一天他买了一批盐，把驴装得能驮多少就驮多少。

sentences.en: On the way home the Ass stumbled as he was crossing a stream and fell into the water.
sentences.zh: 回家路上，驴过小溪时失足跌进了水里。

sentences.en: The salt got thoroughly wetted and much of it melted and drained away …
sentences.zh: 盐全湿透了，大半化掉流走了……

sentences.en: … so that, when he got on his legs again, the Ass found his load had become much less heavy.
sentences.zh: ……所以当驴重新站起来时，发现担子轻了许多。

sentences.en: His master, however, drove him back to town and bought more salt, which he added to what remained in the panniers, and started out again.
sentences.zh: 可是主人把它赶回城里，又买了些盐，加到驮筐里剩下的那部分上，重新出发。

sentences.en: No sooner had they reached a stream than the Ass lay down in it, and rose, as before, with a much lighter load.
sentences.zh: 一到溪边，驴就趴进水里，像上次一样轻了许多地站起来。

sentences.en: But his master detected the trick, and turning back once more, bought a large number of sponges, and piled them on the back of the Ass.
sentences.zh: 可主人看穿了这个把戏，又折回去买了一大堆海绵，堆在驴背上。

sentences.en: When they came to the stream the Ass again lay down …
sentences.zh: 到了溪边，驴又趴了下去……

sentences.en: … but this time, as the sponges soaked up large quantities of water, he found …
sentences.zh: ……可这一次，海绵吸足了水，它发现……

sentences.en: … when he got up on his legs, that he had a bigger burden to carry than ever.
sentences.zh: ……站起来时，背上的担子比先前更重了。

sentences.en: You may play a good card once too often.
sentences.zh: 好牌也有打滥的时候。

title: The Thieves and the Cock
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Some Thieves broke into a house, and found nothing worth taking except a Cock, which they seized and carried off with them.
sentences.zh: 几个盗贼闯进一户人家，除了一只公鸡，没找到什么值得拿的东西，便抓了它带着走了。

sentences.en: When they were preparing their supper, one of them caught up the Cock …
sentences.zh: 他们准备晚饭时，其中一个抓起公鸡……

sentences.en: … and was about to wring his neck, when he cried out for mercy and said, "Pray do not kill me …
sentences.zh: ……正要拧断它的脖子，公鸡求饶道：「请别杀我……」

sentences.en: … you will find me a most useful bird, for I rouse honest men to their work in the morning by my crowing."
sentences.zh: 「……您会发现我是只很有用的鸟，早上我靠打鸣把老实人叫起来干活。」

sentences.en: But the Thief replied with some heat, "Yes, I know you do, making it still harder for us to get a livelihood.
sentences.zh: 可那盗贼有些激动地答道：「是啊，我知道你干这事，这让我们更没法谋生了。

sentences.en: Into the pot you go!"
sentences.zh: 进锅去吧！」

title: The Swollen Fox
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A hungry Fox found in a hollow tree a quantity of bread and meat, which some shepherds had placed there against their return.
sentences.zh: 一只饥饿的狐狸在空心树里发现了一些面包和肉，是几个牧人放在那里留着回来吃的。

sentences.en: Delighted with his find he slipped in through the narrow aperture and greedily devoured it all.
sentences.zh: 它得此发现喜出望外，从窄窄的洞口中钻进去，贪婪地吃了个精光。

sentences.en: But when he tried to get out again he found himself so swollen after his big meal that he could not squeeze through the hole …
sentences.zh: 可当它想再钻出来时，发现饱餐之后肚子胀得那么厉害，怎么也挤不出那个洞了……

sentences.en: … and fell to whining and groaning over his misfortune.
sentences.zh: ……便为自己的倒霉哀声叹气起来。

sentences.en: Another Fox, happening to pass that way, came and asked him what the matter was …
sentences.zh: 另一只狐狸恰好路过，走过来问它怎么了……

sentences.en: … and, on learning the state of the case, said, "Well, my friend, I see nothing for it but for you to stay where you are till you shrink …
sentences.zh: ……弄清原委后说：「唉，朋友，我看没别的办法，你只能待在那儿等瘦下来……」

sentences.en: … to your former size; you'll get out then easily enough."
sentences.zh: 「……瘦回原来的样子，那时要出来就容易了。」

title: The Peasant and the Apple-tree
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Peasant had an Apple-tree growing in his garden, which bore no fruit …
sentences.zh: 一个农夫园子里长着一棵苹果树，它不结果子……

sentences.en: … but merely served to provide a shelter from the heat for the sparrows and grasshoppers which sat and chirped in its branches.
sentences.zh: ……只是给在枝头栖着鸣叫的麻雀和蚱蜢遮遮暑气。

sentences.en: Disappointed at its barrenness he determined to cut it down, and went and fetched his axe for the purpose.
sentences.zh: 他嫌它不结果，便决定砍掉它，为此去取了斧头。

sentences.en: But when the sparrows and the grasshoppers saw what he was about to do, they begged him to spare it …
sentences.zh: 可麻雀和蚱蜢见他要动手，便求他放过这棵树……

sentences.en: … and said to him, "If you destroy the tree we shall have to seek shelter elsewhere …
sentences.zh: ……对他说：「您若毁掉这棵树，我们就得另找栖身之处……」

sentences.en: … and you will no longer have our merry chirping to enliven your work in the garden."
sentences.zh: 「……您在园里干活时，也就再没有我们欢快的鸣叫作伴了。」

sentences.en: He, however, refused to listen to them, and set to work with a will to cut through the trunk.
sentences.zh: 可他不肯听，劲头十足地动手去砍树干。

sentences.en: A few strokes showed that it was hollow inside and contained a swarm of bees and a large store of honey.
sentences.zh: 砍了几斧，便看出里面是空的，藏着一窝蜜蜂和大量蜂蜜。

sentences.en: Delighted with his find he threw down his axe, saying, "The old tree is worth keeping after all."
sentences.zh: 他因这发现大喜，扔下斧头说：「这棵老树终究还是值得留着的。」

sentences.en: Utility is most men's test of worth.
sentences.zh: 对多数人来说，有用才算有价值。

title: The Jackdaw and the Pigeons
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Jackdaw, watching some Pigeons in a farmyard, was filled with envy when he saw how well they were fed …
sentences.zh: 一只寒鸦看着农家院子里的几只鸽子，见它们吃得多好，满心羡慕……

sentences.en: … and determined to disguise himself as one of them, in order to secure a share of the good things they enjoyed.
sentences.zh: ……便决意伪装成它们中的一员，好分得一份它们享受的好处。

sentences.en: So he painted himself white from head to foot and joined the flock …
sentences.zh: 于是他从头到脚把自己涂成白色，混进了鸽群……

sentences.en: … and, so long as he was silent, they never suspected that he was not a pigeon like themselves.
sentences.zh: ……只要他不作声，鸽子们从没怀疑过他其实不是同类。

sentences.en: But one day he was unwise enough to start chattering …
sentences.zh: 可是有一天他不小心开口叫了起来……

sentences.en: … when they at once saw through his disguise and pecked him so unmercifully that he was glad to escape and join his own kind again.
sentences.zh: ……鸽子们立刻看穿了他的伪装，毫不留情地啄他，他只好赶紧逃回去找同类。

sentences.en: But the other jackdaws did not recognise him in his white dress, and would not let him feed with them, but drove him away …
sentences.zh: 可别的寒鸦认不出他这身白装，不让他一起觅食，把他赶走了……

sentences.en: … and so he became a homeless wanderer for his pains.
sentences.zh: ……于是他白费心机，成了无家可归的流浪者。

title: Jupiter and the Tortoise
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Jupiter was about to marry a wife, and determined to celebrate the event by inviting all the animals to a banquet.
sentences.zh: 朱庇特要娶妻了，决定宴请所有动物来庆祝这件喜事。

sentences.en: They all came except the Tortoise, who did not put in an appearance, much to Jupiter's surprise.
sentences.zh: 大家都来了，唯独乌龟没有露面，这让朱庇特很意外。

sentences.en: So when he next saw the Tortoise he asked him why he had not been at the banquet.
sentences.zh: 所以下次见到乌龟时，他便问它为什么没来赴宴。

sentences.en: "I don't care for going out," said the Tortoise; "there's no place like home."
sentences.zh: 「我不爱出门，」乌龟说，「哪儿都不如家里好。」

sentences.en: Jupiter was so much annoyed by this reply that he decreed that from that time forth the Tortoise should carry his house upon his back …
sentences.zh: 朱庇特被这个回答弄得很恼火，便规定从今往后乌龟要把房子背在背上……

sentences.en: … and never be able to get away from home even if he wished to.
sentences.zh: ……即便想离开家也永远走不脱了。

title: The Stag at the Pool
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A thirsty Stag went down to a pool to drink.
sentences.zh: 一只口渴的雄鹿下到池塘边喝水。

sentences.en: As he bent over the surface he saw his own reflection in the water, and was struck with admiration for his fine spreading antlers …
sentences.zh: 它俯身水面时看见自己的倒影，为自己舒展华美的鹿角赞叹不已……

sentences.en: … but at the same time he felt nothing but disgust for the weakness and slenderness of his legs.
sentences.zh: ……可同时又嫌自己的腿细弱无力，只觉得厌恶。

sentences.en: While he stood there looking at himself, he was seen and attacked by a Lion …
sentences.zh: 它站在那里自顾自看时，被一头狮子看见了，遭到袭击……

sentences.en: … but in the chase which ensued, he soon drew away from his pursuer …
sentences.zh: ……可在随后的追逐中，它很快就甩开了追它的东西……

sentences.en: … and kept his lead as long as the ground over which he ran was open and free of trees.
sentences.zh: ……只要跑过的是开阔无树的地方，它就一直领先。

sentences.en: But coming presently to a wood, he was caught by his antlers in the branches, and fell a victim to the teeth and claws of his enemy.
sentences.zh: 可不久进了树林，它的鹿角卡在树枝里，终于死在仇敌的牙爪之下。

sentences.en: "Woe is me!" he cried with his last breath …
sentences.zh: 「我真是苦啊！」它用最后一口气叫道……

sentences.en: … "I despised my legs, which might have saved my life: but I gloried in my horns, and they have proved my ruin."
sentences.zh: 「……我嫌弃自己的腿，而它本可以救我性命；我引以为荣的角，倒成了我的祸根。」

sentences.en: What is worth most is often valued least.
sentences.zh: 最有价值的东西，往往最不被看重。

title: Hercules and the Waggoner
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Waggoner was driving his team along a muddy lane with a full load behind them …
sentences.zh: 一个车夫赶着一队牲口走在泥泞的小路上，后面载着满满的货物……

sentences.en: … when the wheels of his waggon sank so deep in the mire that no efforts of his horses could move them.
sentences.zh: ……车轮陷进泥里太深，他的马怎么使劲也拉不动。

sentences.en: As he stood there, looking helplessly on, and calling loudly at intervals upon Hercules for assistance, the god himself appeared …
sentences.zh: 他站在那儿无助地看着，不时高喊求赫拉克勒斯相助，这时那位神亲自出现了……

sentences.en: … and said to him, "Put your shoulder to the wheel, man, and goad on your horses, and then you may call on Hercules to assist you.
sentences.zh: ……对他说：「汉子，先把肩膀顶上车轮，把马赶起来，然后你再求赫拉克勒斯帮忙。

sentences.en: If you won't lift a finger to help yourself, you can't expect Hercules or any one else to come to your aid."
sentences.zh: 你要是不肯动一根手指帮自己，就别指望赫拉克勒斯或任何人来帮你。」

sentences.en: Heaven helps those who help themselves.
sentences.zh: 天助自助者。

title: Mercury and the Sculptor
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Mercury was very anxious to know in what estimation he was held by mankind …
sentences.zh: 墨丘利很想知道人类对他评价如何……

sentences.en: … so he disguised himself as a man and walked into a Sculptor's studio, where there were a number of statues finished and ready for sale.
sentences.zh: ……于是化身为人，走进一位雕刻师的工作室，那里摆着许多已完工待售的雕像。

sentences.en: Seeing a statue of Jupiter among the rest, he inquired the price of it.
sentences.zh: 他在其中看见一尊朱庇特的像，便问价钱。

sentences.en: "A crown," said the Sculptor.
sentences.zh: 「一克朗。」雕刻师说。

sentences.en: "Is that all?" said he, laughing; "and" (pointing to one of Juno) "how much is that one?"
sentences.zh: 「就这些？」他笑着说，「那么」（指着一尊朱诺像）「那一尊多少？」

sentences.en: "That," was the reply, "is half a crown."
sentences.zh: 「那尊，」对方答道，「半克朗。」

sentences.en: "And how much might you be wanting for that one over there, now?" he continued, pointing to a statue of himself.
sentences.zh: 「那么那边那一尊，你要多少钱呢？」他接着问，指着自己的一尊像。

sentences.en: "That one?" said the Sculptor; "Oh, I'll throw him in for nothing if you'll buy the other two."
sentences.zh: 「那一尊？」雕刻师说，「哦，您要是买下另外两尊，这个我就白送。」

title: The Frogs Asking for a King
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Time was when the Frogs were discontented because they had no one to rule over them …
sentences.zh: 从前，青蛙们因为没有人统治它们而心怀不满……

sentences.en: … so they sent a deputation to Jupiter to ask him to give them a King.
sentences.zh: ……于是派了个代表团去见朱庇特，求他给它们一位国王。

sentences.en: Jupiter, despising the folly of their request, cast a log into the pool where they lived, and said that that should be their King.
sentences.zh: 朱庇特觉得这请求愚不可及，便往它们住的池塘里扔了一根木头，说这就是它们的国王。

sentences.en: The Frogs were terrified at first by the splash, and scuttled away into the deepest parts of the pool …
sentences.zh: 青蛙们起初被水花吓坏了，慌忙逃进池塘最深处……

sentences.en: … but by and by, when they saw that the log remained motionless, one by one they ventured to the surface again …
sentences.zh: ……可过了一会儿，见那木头一动不动，便一只只又壮着胆子浮上来……

sentences.en: … and before long, growing bolder, they began to feel such contempt for it that they even took to sitting upon it.
sentences.zh: ……不久胆子更大，竟对它生出轻蔑之心，甚至爬上去坐着。

sentences.en: Thinking that a King of that sort was an insult to their dignity, they sent to Jupiter a second time …
sentences.zh: 它们觉得这样一位国王侮辱了它们的尊严，便第二次派人去见朱庇特……

sentences.en: … and begged him to take away the sluggish King he had given them, and to give them another and a better one.
sentences.zh: ……求他把赐给它们的这位呆滞国王收回去，另给一位更好的。

sentences.en: Jupiter, annoyed at being pestered in this way, sent a Stork to rule over them …
sentences.zh: 朱庇特被这样纠缠得恼了，便派一只鹳去统治它们……

sentences.en: … who no sooner arrived among them than he began to catch and eat the Frogs as fast as he could.
sentences.zh: ……那鹳一到它们中间，便拼命地抓青蛙来吃。

title: The Peacock and Juno
author: Aesop

sentences.en: The Peacock was greatly discontented because he had not a beautiful voice like the nightingale …
sentences.zh: 孔雀因为没有夜莺那样动听的歌喉，十分不满……

sentences.en: … and he went and complained to Juno about it.
sentences.zh: ……便去向她朱诺抱怨。

sentences.en: "The nightingale's song," said he, "is the envy of all the birds; but whenever I utter a sound I become a laughing-stock."
sentences.zh: 「夜莺的歌声，」他说，「叫所有的鸟都羡慕；可我一开口，就成了笑柄。」

sentences.en: The goddess tried to console him by saying, "You have not, it is true, the power of song, but then you far excel all the rest in beauty …
sentences.zh: 女神安慰他说：「你确实没有歌唱的本事，可你在美貌上远胜过其余所有……」

sentences.en: … your neck flashes like the emerald and your splendid tail is a marvel of gorgeous colour."
sentences.zh: 「……你的颈项闪亮如翡翠，你那华美的尾羽更是斑斓夺目的奇观。」

sentences.en: But the Peacock was not appeased.
sentences.zh: 可孔雀并未因此平息。

sentences.en: "What is the use," said he, "of being beautiful, with a voice like mine?"
sentences.zh: 「生得这么美，」他说，「配上我这样的嗓子，又有什么用？」

sentences.en: Then Juno replied, with a shade of sternness in her tones, "Fate has allotted to all their destined gifts …
sentences.zh: 朱诺便带着几分严厉答道：「命运已给众生各分了应得的禀赋……」

sentences.en: … to yourself beauty, to the eagle strength, to the nightingale song, and so on to all the rest in their degree …
sentences.zh: 「……给你美貌，给鹰力量，给夜莺歌声，其余诸类也各按本分……」

sentences.en: … but you alone are dissatisfied with your portion.
sentences.zh: 「……只有你对自己那一份不满。

sentences.en: Make, then, no more complaints.
sentences.zh: 既如此，就不要再抱怨了。

sentences.en: For, if your present wish were granted, you would quickly find cause for fresh discontent."
sentences.zh: 因为假若你眼下的愿望得以实现，你很快又会找到新的不满之由。」

title: The Lion, the Bear, and the Fox
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Lion and a Bear were fighting for possession of a kid, which they had both seized at the same moment.
sentences.zh: 一头狮子和一头熊为争夺一只小山羊而厮打，它们同时抓住了它。

sentences.en: The battle was long and fierce, and at length both of them were exhausted …
sentences.zh: 这场恶斗又久又猛烈，到最后两个都力气耗尽……

sentences.en: … and lay upon the ground severely wounded and gasping for breath.
sentences.zh: ……倒在地上，伤得很重，喘息不止。

sentences.en: A Fox had all the time been prowling round and watching the fight …
sentences.zh: 一只狐狸一直在周围徘徊，看着这场打斗……

sentences.en: … and when he saw the combatants lying there too weak to move, he slipped in and seized the kid, and ran off with it.
sentences.zh: ……见两个斗士躺在那儿连动的力气都没有，便溜进去抓起小羊跑掉了。

sentences.en: They looked on helplessly, and one said to the other, "Here we've been mauling each other all this while …
sentences.zh: 它们无可奈何地看着，其中一个对另一个说：「我们厮打了这么久……」

sentences.en: … and no one the better for it except the Fox!"
sentences.zh: 「……结果除了狐狸，谁也没捞着好处！」

title: The Two Soldiers and the Robber
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Two Soldiers travelling together were set upon by a Robber.
sentences.zh: 两个同行的士兵遭到一个强盗袭击。

sentences.en: One of them ran away, but the other stood his ground …
sentences.zh: 其中一个跑了，另一个却站住不退……

sentences.en: … and laid about him so lustily with his sword that the Robber was fain to fly and leave him in peace.
sentences.zh: ……挥剑奋勇砍杀，强盗只好逃走，不再惹他。

sentences.en: When the coast was clear the timid one ran back, and, flourishing his weapon, cried in a threatening voice, "Where is he?
sentences.zh: 危险过去后，那个胆小的跑回来，挥舞着兵器，用威胁的口吻叫道：「他在哪儿？

sentences.en: Let me get at him, and I'll soon let him know whom he's got to deal with."
sentences.zh: 让我去会他，我很快就让他知道惹的是谁。」

sentences.en: But the other replied, "You are a little late, my friend …
sentences.zh: 可另一个答道：「朋友，你来得晚了点……」

sentences.en: … I only wish you had backed me up just now, even if you had done no more than speak …
sentences.zh: 「……我只盼你刚才能给我撑腰，哪怕只是说句话也好……」

sentences.en: … for I should have been encouraged, believing your words to be true.
sentences.zh: 「……那样我也会受些鼓舞，以为你的话是真的。

sentences.en: As it is, calm yourself, and put up your sword: there is no further use for it.
sentences.zh: 事已如此，你安静些，把剑收起来吧，它已经没用了。

sentences.en: You may delude others into thinking you're as brave as a lion: but I know that, at the first sign of danger, you run away like a hare."
sentences.zh: 你或许能骗别人相信你勇猛如狮；可我知道，一有危险，你跑得比兔子还快。」

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Wolf, the Mother, and Her Child
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A hungry Wolf was prowling about in search of food.
sentences.zh: 一只饥饿的狼四处游荡觅食。

sentences.en: By and by, attracted by the cries of a Child, he came to a cottage.
sentences.zh: 不久，他被一个孩子的哭声引来，来到一间小屋前。

sentences.en: As he crouched beneath the window, he heard the Mother say to the Child, "Stop crying, do! or I'll throw you to the Wolf."
sentences.zh: 他蹲在窗下，听见母亲对孩子说：「别哭了！再哭就把你扔给狼。」

sentences.en: Thinking she really meant what she said, he waited there a long time in the expectation of satisfying his hunger.
sentences.zh: 他以为她当真如此，便在那儿等了很久，指望能填饱肚子。

sentences.en: In the evening he heard the Mother fondling her Child and saying, "If the naughty Wolf comes, he shan't get my little one …
sentences.zh: 到了晚上，他听见母亲爱抚着孩子说：「要是那坏狼敢来，他休想碰我的小宝贝……」

sentences.en: … Daddy will kill him."
sentences.zh: 「……爸爸会打死他。」

sentences.en: The Wolf got up in much disgust and walked away …
sentences.zh: 狼十分厌恶地起身走开……

sentences.en: … "As for the people in that house," said he to himself, "you can't believe a word they say."
sentences.zh: ……「那一家人，」他自言自语，「说的话一个字都不能信。」

title: The Cat and the Cock
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Cat pounced on a Cock, and cast about for some good excuse for making a meal off him, for Cats don't as a rule eat Cocks …
sentences.zh: 一只猫扑住一只公鸡，琢磨着找个好借口把他吃掉，因为猫通常并不吃公鸡……

sentences.en: … and she knew she ought not to.
sentences.zh: ……她也知道自己不该如此。

sentences.en: At last she said, "You make a great nuisance of yourself at night by crowing and keeping people awake …
sentences.zh: 最后她说：「你夜里打鸣，吵得人睡不着，实在讨厌……」

sentences.en: … so I am going to make an end of you."
sentences.zh: 「……所以我要结果了你。」

sentences.en: But the Cock defended himself by saying that he crowed in order that men might wake up and set about the day's work in good time …
sentences.zh: 公鸡为自己辩解说，他打鸣是为了让人们醒来、按时开始一天的活儿……

sentences.en: … and that they really couldn't very well do without him.
sentences.zh: ……人们实在少不得他。

sentences.en: "That may be," said the Cat, "but whether they can or not, I'm not going without my dinner"; and she killed and ate him.
sentences.zh: 「也许吧，」猫说，「可不管他们少不少得，我总不能不吃晚饭。」说完就把他弄死吃了。

sentences.en: The want of a good excuse never kept a villain from crime.
sentences.zh: 恶人从不会因为找不到好借口就不作恶。

source: Aesop, Aesop's Fables, trans. V. S. Vernon Jones (1912). 英文原文为公版作品（Project Gutenberg eBook #11339，https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/11339），无版权限制；中文译文由本项目人工翻译，采用与仓库一致的 MIT 许可。原文过长处按分句截断并以省略号（…）标注，前后两半拼接即原句，不增删任何词。

title: The Hare and the Tortoise
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Hare was one day making fun of a Tortoise for being so slow upon his feet.
sentences.zh: 有一天，一只兔子嘲笑乌龟走路太慢。

sentences.en: "Wait a bit," said the Tortoise; "I'll run a race with you, and I'll wager that I win."
sentences.zh: 「等着瞧吧，」乌龟说，「我跟你赛跑，我还敢打赌我能赢。」

sentences.en: "Oh, well," replied the Hare, who was much amused at the idea, "let's try and see" …
sentences.zh: 「哦，好啊，」兔子觉得这主意十分可笑，答道，「那就试试看吧……」

sentences.en: … and it was soon agreed that the fox should set a course for them, and be the judge.
sentences.zh: ……很快便商定由狐狸给他们划定赛道，并当裁判。

sentences.en: When the time came both started off together, but the Hare was soon so far ahead that he thought he might as well have a rest …
sentences.zh: 比赛开始时两个一同出发，可兔子很快就跑得远远领先，觉得不妨歇一歇……

sentences.en: … so down he lay and fell fast asleep.
sentences.zh: ……于是躺下便睡熟了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile the Tortoise kept plodding on, and in time reached the goal.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，乌龟一直艰难而稳步地走，终于到了终点。

sentences.en: At last the Hare woke up with a start, and dashed on at his fastest, but only to find that the Tortoise had already won the race.
sentences.zh: 最后兔子猛地醒来，以最快的速度冲出去，却发现乌龟早已赢了比赛。

sentences.en: Slow and steady wins the race.
sentences.zh: 稳扎稳打，方能取胜。

title: The Soldier and His Horse
author: Aesop

sentences.en: A Soldier gave his Horse a plentiful supply of oats in time of war, and tended him with the utmost care …
sentences.zh: 战争时期，一名士兵给他的马充足的燕麦，照料得极为精心……

sentences.en: … for he wished him to be strong to endure the hardships of the field …
sentences.zh: ……因为他希望它强壮得能熬住战场的艰苦……

sentences.en: … and swift to bear his master, when need arose, out of the reach of danger.
sentences.zh: ……并在需要时迅速把主人带离险境。

sentences.en: But when the war was over he employed him on all sorts of drudgery, bestowing but little attention upon him …
sentences.zh: 可战争一结束，他便让马干各种粗活，很少再过问它……

sentences.en: … and giving him, moreover, nothing but chaff to eat.
sentences.zh: ……而且只给它谷壳吃。

sentences.en: The time came when war broke out again, and the Soldier saddled and bridled his Horse, and, having put on his heavy coat of mail, mounted …
sentences.zh: 战事又起的日子到了，士兵给马配上鞍辔，穿上沉重的铠甲，跨上……

sentences.en: … him to ride off and take the field.
sentences.zh: 「……马背，要骑它上阵。

sentences.en: But the poor half-starved beast sank down under his weight, and said to his rider, "You will have to go into battle on foot this time.
sentences.zh: 可这头饿得半死的可怜牲口在他身下瘫倒了，对骑手说：「这一回你只好步行上阵了。

sentences.en: Thanks to hard work and bad food, you have turned me from a Horse into an ass …
sentences.zh: 多亏重活和劣食，你已把我从一匹马变成了一头驴……」

sentences.en: … and you cannot in a moment turn me back again into a Horse."
sentences.zh: 「……而你不能一下子又把我变回马去。」

title: The Oxen and the Butchers
author: Aesop

sentences.en: Once upon a time the Oxen determined to be revenged upon the Butchers for the havoc they wrought in their ranks …
sentences.zh: 从前，公牛们决定向屠夫报仇，因为屠夫在它们中间大肆杀戳……

sentences.en: … and plotted to put them to death on a given day.
sentences.zh: ……并密谋在约定的日子把他们弄死。

sentences.en: They were all gathered together discussing how best to carry out the plan …
sentences.zh: 它们聚在一起商议怎样最好地施行这个计划……

sentences.en: … and the more violent of them were engaged in sharpening their horns for the fray …
sentences.zh: ……其中较激烈的一些已在磨角，准备厮杀……

sentences.en: … when an old Ox got up upon his feet and said, "My brothers, you have good reason, I know, to hate these Butchers, but, at any rate …
sentences.zh: ……这时一头老公牛站起来说：「弟兄们，我知道你们恨这些屠夫有理，可无论如何……」

sentences.en: … they understand their trade and do what they have to do without causing unnecessary pain.
sentences.zh: 「……他们懂本行，该做的事做得干净，不叫人多受无谓的痛苦。

sentences.en: But if we kill them, others, who have no experience, will be set to slaughter us …
sentences.zh: 可我们若杀了他们，派来宰我们的就是些没经验的生手……」

sentences.en: … and will by their bungling inflict great sufferings upon us.
sentences.zh: 「……他们会因笨拙而给我们带来极大的苦楚。

sentences.en: For you may be sure that, even though all the Butchers perish, mankind will never go without their beef."
sentences.zh: 你们尽可放心，即便屠夫全死光了，人类也绝不会吃不上牛肉。」
